Home — The Millennium Prize Problems
In order to celebrate mathematics in the new millennium, The Clay Mathematics Institute of Cambridge, Massachusetts (CMI) established seven Prize Problems.
The Prizes were conceived to record some of the most difficult problems with which mathematicians were grappling at the turn of the second millennium; to elevate in the consciousness of the general public the fact that in mathematics, the frontier is still open and abounds in important unsolved problems; to emphasize the importance of working towards a solution of the deepest, most difficult problems; and to recognize achievement in mathematics of historical magnitude.
The prizes were announced at a meeting in Paris, held on May 24, 2000 at the Collège de France.
Three lectures were presented: Timothy Gowers spoke on The Importance of Mathematics; Michael Atiyah and John Tate spoke on the problems themselves.
The seven Millennium Prize Problems were chosen by the founding Scientific Advisory Board of CMI, which conferred with leading experts worldwide.
The focus of the board was on important classic questions that have resisted solution for many years.
Following the decision of the Scientific Advisory Board, the Board of Directors of CMI designated a $7 million prize fund for the solutions to these problems, with $1 million allocated to the solution of each problem.
It is of note that one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, the Riemann hypothesis, formulated in 1859, also appears in the list of twenty-three problems discussed in the address given in Paris by David Hilbert on August 9, 1900.
The rules for the award of the prize have the endorsement of the CMI Scientific Advisory Board and the approval of the Directors.
The members of these boards have the responsibility to preserve the nature, the integrity, and the spirit of this prize.

If we stretch a rubber band around the surface of an apple, then we can shrink it down to a point by moving it slowly, without tearing it and without allowing it to leave the surface.
On the other hand, if we imagine that the same rubber band has somehow been stretched in the appropriate direction around a doughnut, then there is no way of shrinking it to a point without breaking either the rubber band or the doughnut.
We say the surface of the apple is “simply connected,” but that the surface of the doughnut is not.
Poincaré, almost a hundred years ago, knew that a two dimensional sphere is essentially characterized by this property of simple connectivity, and asked the corresponding question for the three dimensional sphere.
This question turned out to be extraordinarily difficult.
Nearly a century passed between its formulation in 1904 by Henri Poincaré and its solution by Grigoriy Perelman, announced in preprints posted on ArXiv.org in 2002 and 2003.
Perelman’s solution was based on Richard Hamilton’s theory of Ricci flow, and made use of results on spaces of metrics due to Cheeger, Gromov, and Perelman himself.
In these papers Perelman also proved William Thurston’s Geometrization Conjecture, a special case of which is the Poincaré conjecture.
See the press release of March 18, 2010.

Washington Post: A reclusive Russian mathematician, Grigori Perelman, who three months ago was awarded the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize for proving the Poincaré conjecture, yesterday turned down the award and the $1 million prize.
Perelman, who quit his job at the Steklov Institute and lives with his elderly mother in St.
Petersburg, has in the past turned down a number of other mathematics awards, including the most prestigious of all, the Fields medal.
His 1988 sketch of how to use Antarctic ice to detect neutrinos led to the IceCube observatory, which made the first detections of high-energy neutrinos in 2013.

[Submitted on 11 Nov 2002]
Title:The entropy formula for the Ricci flow and its geometric applications
View PDF HTML (experimental)
Abstract: We present a monotonic expression for the Ricci flow, valid in all dimensions and without curvature assumptions.
It is interpreted as an entropy for a certain canonical ensemble.
Several geometric applications are given.
In particular, (1) Ricci flow, considered on the space of riemannian metrics modulo diffeomorphism and scaling, has no nontrivial periodic orbits (that is, other than fixed points); (2) In a region, where singularity is forming in finite time, the injectivity radius is controlled by the curvature; (3) Ricci flow can not quickly turn an almost euclidean region into a very curved one, no matter what happens far away.

On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
We’re sharing a solution to the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the Millennium Prize Problems.
This proof, produced by an internal OpenAI system, shows that the dynamics of the Navier-Stokes equations for fluid motion can develop a singularity in finite time.
We’re sharing both a writeup of the proof and a formalization in Lean.
The Millennium Prize Problems(opens in a new window) represent some of the deepest questions at the frontier of mathematics.
The question of whether smooth three-dimensional fluid motion can break down has remained unresolved for roughly 90 years.
A major goal of our work is to empower scientists to advance research and technology that benefits all of humanity.
To solve the Navier–Stokes problem, we used an internal model that is significantly more capable than GPT‑6 Astra.
We believe it is important to inform the world about the pace of AI progress and what to expect from upcoming models.
The Navier–Stokes equations use Newton’s second law of motion (“F=ma”) to describe how fluids move.
Importantly, they treat a fluid as a continuous medium rather than tracking individual molecules.
These equations are used for aircraft design, weather forecasting, and the study of blood flow.
A fundamental open question for these dynamical equations has been whether the continuum approximation of the fluid can break down.
Specifically, can the Navier–Stokes equations for a three-dimensional incompressible fluid with constant density develop a “singularity,” even when the motion starts smoothly?
Here, a singularity means the dynamics lead to speeds in the fluid growing without bound within a finite amount of time.
The development of a singularity would have to happen despite the presence of viscosity, which tends to smooth out motion.
Because a real fluid cannot move infinitely fast, this would mark a breakdown in how the equations model the fluid.
To continue modeling the system, one would then need to track the behaviour of each particle individually.
The equations date to the nineteenth-century work of Claude-Louis Navier and George Gabriel Stokes.
In 1934, Jean Leray proved that solutions exist in a generalized sense, but whether they always remain smooth became a central unanswered question.
In 2000, the Clay Mathematics Institute named the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem one of seven Millennium Prize Problems.
Our system produced an analytical proof and a Lean formalization that an initially smooth fluid at rest can develop a singularity in a finite time.
The fluid has a smooth force applied to it, and its energy remains finite through the entire dynamics, from rest to the formation of the singularity.
This resolves the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize problem by establishing statement “C” (and also “D”) in the official Millennium Prize formulation(opens in a new window).
The solution is a vortex, a spinning swirl of fluid, that spirals inward and gets increasingly elongated, like spaghetti.
This central region shrinks while it speeds up in such a way that its energy still stays finite, as required by the laws of physics.
The technical challenge is for the equations to develop the breakdown through the motion of the fluid itself, rather than, for example, us putting in an infinite force by hand.
More mathematically, the terms in the Navier–Stokes equations that describe the motion—acceleration, pressure gradients, momentum transfer, viscosity—must both become big yet cancel in a precise way.
This detailed balance leaves a smooth external force even as the velocity of the fluid grows without bound.
Since August 28 we have been training a new internal model that has exhibited unprecedented performance in our benchmarks, including mathematics.
This model’s training is ongoing and its performance continues to improve.
On Tuesday, September 1, we heard rumors that two Millennium Prize problem
[...]
er equations, and our agents surprised us by resolving this question.
The specific variant of the question that they resolved was the unforced version, where no external force is applied to the fluid.
Nearly 100 agents worked together for approximately 50 hours to produce our Euler regularity disproof.
Once we saw the Euler solution, we thought that Navier–Stokes was the most promising problem to work on.
Thus, we decided to devote our resources to Navier–Stokes.
To do so, we shifted agents away from the other Millennium Problems and prompted these agents with the Euler resolution.
When a further trained version of our internal model became available over the course of the effort, we updated our agents to that model.
We encouraged different groups of agents to explore a diversity of approaches.
After some time, we cross-pollinated the agent groups by using Codex to consolidate the most useful insights from each agent group.
These follow-up prompts drew on the agents’ own intermediate results.
The group that found the solution to Navier–Stokes was guided in such a way.
The agents arrived at their resolution on Saturday, September 5, about 88 hours after the first agents were launched.
Lean formalization and verification took an additional 17 hours via GPT‑6 Astra.
Across all attempted problems, the agents sent 4.9 million messages and used about 300 billion output tokens.
In the process of resolving the Navier–Stokes problem, the agents sent 2.7 million messages and used approximately 130 billion output tokens.
Our effort began on September 1st after hearing a rumor which we later realized was related to Levent Alpöge, an Anthropic employee, and Tristan Buckmaster, a math professor at NYU.
After the completion of our full project and Lean verification (on September 6th), believing from the rumor they also had a solution of Navier–Stokes, we reached out to them to offer a concurrent release of our result and to recognize their priority in a joint announcement.
At that point we found out that, using an internal Anthropic model, they had produced a resolution of the forced Euler problem.
In these discussions we offered them visibility into all of the prompts we used and later to see the proof.
We recognize the priority of their work on forced Euler and congratulate them on their remarkable mathematical achievement.
We (the researchers and the agents) did not see any of their work through any means until they released it publicly — in particular, no specific user data was accessed in order to solve this problem.
Following an investigation, we have confirmed that Buckmaster’s Codex prompts over the two months preceding this announcement and paper on September 8, 2026, could not have influenced the system in any way, including through training.
The OpenAI internal model used for this result was developed through large-scale reinforcement learning on top of a previously pretrained model.
Our proofs also differ significantly.
In the Euler case, Alpöge and Buckmaster proved a result with external forcing, while OpenAI’s system proved a result without external forcing.
Our goal in releasing this result is to report on the substantial progress of our AI models.
We do not intend to claim the Millennium Prize for this result.
This milestone represents substantial work by mathematicians and AI researchers.
However, this is not a culmination, but rather a snapshot in time, of progress

27 October 2026
OpenAI's Navier-Stokes proof called into question
Attempts by OpenAI to solve a major mathematical mystery have raised questions about whether AI-generated mathematical arguments can be reliably translated into a form that computers can check.
The Navier-Stokes equations help describe how fluids such as water and air move, but have puzzled mathematicians for centuries.
Solving them would be a significant mathematical achievement.
In a new pre-print, King’s College London and the University of Cambridge mathematicians discovered that the version of OpenAI’s Navier-Stokes proof written in a programming language designed to verify mathematical proofs does not fully match the proof published for human mathematicians.
While the finding does not yet establish that OpenAI’s original proof is incorrect, or that its claimed mathematical result is wrong, it suggests that the written proof and its computer-verified version make different mathematical claims.
This means that verifying the formal version alone cannot establish that the original written proof has been correctly represented and checked.
Dr Alexander Bastounis, co-author of the paper, and Lecturer in Applied Mathematics, King’s College London, said: “OpenAI’s struggle to accurately translate its proofs into a machine-checkable language highlights a broader challenge: verifying the correctness of the output of an AI remains exceptionally difficult.”
The research is reported in a preprint published on arXiv.
The paper has not yet undergone peer review.
In September 2026, OpenAI announced that its AI systems had produced a proof showing that such a breakdown can occur under certain conditions, addressing the longstanding mathematical problem.
The company published two versions of its proof: one written in conventional mathematical language and notation, and another in Lean, a programming language used to check mathematical arguments.
Mathematical proofs
[...]
owever, this does not automatically establish that a separate proof written in conventional mathematical language makes the same mathematical claims.
Computer verification can establish whether a written proof is correct if that proof has been correctly translated into a formal language.
The challenge is establishing that the translation is accurate.
Lean code is designed primarily to enable machines to verify mathematical arguments, making it unsuitable for mathematicians to readily scrutinise the reasoning or use the results in their own research.
Researchers therefore need to be able to scrutinise the original mathematical argument, as well as establish that any computer-verified version faithfully represents it.
Drawing on their work investigating the limitations of AI, the researchers questioned whether OpenAI’s written proof had been translated accurately into Lean.
When the researchers compared the two versions of OpenAI’s proof, they found several places where they did not match.
In one example, the written proof makes a claim that is stronger than the corresponding claim in the computer-checked version.
In other words, the two versions do not quite say the same thing.
The researchers have not shown that OpenAI’s original proof is wrong.
Instead, their findings show that a computer confirming that a Lean proof is logically correct does not guarantee that the Lean proof matches the argument written for mathematicians to read.
The written proof still needs to be checked independently to establish whether its reasoning is correct.
Their analysis also reveals a deeper problem: there is no general way to automatically translate mathematical arguments written for humans into a form that computers can verify.
The researchers used a mathematical framework called the Solvability Complexity Index (SCI) hierarchy, which helps classify computational problems according to how they can be solved by computers, including whether they can be solved using a reliable, step-by-step process.
Their findings reveal a fundamental limit to automatically translating mathematical arguments written for humans into proofs that computers can verify.

The S&P U.S.
Indices are a family of equity indices designed to measure the market performance of U.S.

The family is composed of a wide range of indices based on
size, sector, and style.
The indices are weighted by float-adjusted market capitalization (FMC).
In

market and includes
all eligible U.S.

market.

Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 3.4 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the advance estimate released today by the U.S.
Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA).
In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent.
The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports.
Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased.
For more information, refer to the "Technical Notes" below.
Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports.
Imports increased more in the third quarter than in the second quarter.
Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, the sum of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased 4.9 percent in the third quarter, compared with an increase of 4.6 percent in the second quarter.
The price index for gross domestic purchases increased 3.0 percent in the third quarter, compared with an increase of 5.6 percent in the second quarter.
The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index increased 2.1 percent, compared with an increase of 5.0 percent, and the PCE price index, excluding food and energy increased 2.5 percent, compared with an increase of 3.3 percent.

quotes: The raw rank is simply the rank of the model's Arena score.
Therefore, two models are tied if their rank spreads overlap.
polymarket-4664495.text:
The raw rank is simply the rank of the model's Arena score.
Therefore, two models are tied if their rank spreads overlap.

Today, we are announcing an update to our ranking methodology that makes our rankings both more interpretable and more accurate in how they reflect statistical uncertainty.
We are grateful to our community members for helpful suggestions that have led to this decision.
Alongside each model score, we are now reporting the raw rank and the rank spread for the respective model.
The raw rank is simply the rank of the model's Arena score.
There are no ties in the rank column: each model is assigned a unique rank.
Models in the leaderboard are sorted based on the raw rank.
Ties are reflected in the rank spread, which is an interval whose lower and upper endpoints correspond to the best and worst rank a model could have, based on all models' confidence intervals (CIs).
The scores and confidence intervals remain unchanged.
Formally, the best rank a model M can have is 1 + #{models whose lower CI endpoint is greater than model M's upper CI endpoint} .
Analogously, the worst rank a model M can have is 1 + #{models whose upper CI endpoint is greater than model M's lower CI endpoint} .
(The "1+" ensures that ranks cannot be zero; the best possible rank is one.)
Intuitively, one can interpret the rank spread as follows.
Suppose the true Arena score of model M is equal to the highest value included in its score's CI, and suppose that the true scores of all other models are the lowest values included in their respective CIs.
This "optimistic" rank is the lower endpoint of model M's rank spread.
The "pessimistic" rank is obtained analogously, by assuming model M's score is the lowest value included in its CI and all other models' scores are the highest values in their respective CIs.
This is the upper endpoint of model M's rank spread.
Therefore, two models are tied if their rank spreads overlap.
The raw ranking is the current best estimate of the true underlying ranking.
For example, in the screenshot above, gemini-2.5-pro , claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-thinking-32k, claude-opus-4-1-20250805-thinking-16k , and claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 are all contenders for the number one spot because their rank spread includes 1.
However, based on current data our best estimate is that gemini-2.5-pro has the highest true underlying score.
Previously, we only reported the "optimistic" rank, i.e.
the lower endpoint of the rank spread, as described above.
This methodology naturally assigned high ranks to models whose scores have high uncertainty, i.e.
large CIs (for example, new models on the leaderboard).
The new ranking method is more neutral, placing equal emphasis on the "optimistic" and the "pessimistic" ranking implied by the CIs.

Hangzhou, China, November 16, 2026 - Alibaba has released Qwen4-Max, the most capable model in the Qwen family to date.
Featuring 2.4 trillion total parameters, native vision capabilities, and a one-million-token context window, Qwen4-Max excels at complex tasks across work, creativity, and research.
Qwen4-Max achieves top rankings across leading benchmarks, particularly in coding, agentic tasks and visual reasoning.
It ranked 6th on Code Arena, a real-world coding leaderboard, and posted strong scores across specialized benchmarks for agent workflows, workplace productivity, and visual reasoning, including Agents' Last Exam, Vals Index, JobBench, and Chartography.
According to Work360—a proprietary benchmark evaluating performance on challenging industry tasks across 721 specialized fields—Qwen4-Max outperforms its predecessor, Qwen3.8-Max, overall while using 35% fewer tokens at High effort reasoning mode and reducing the average cost per task by around 60%.
These gains are driven by the new Qwen4 architecture, which upgrades the sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) design across attention, residual connections, and embeddings.
Built as an MoE model with 2.4 trillion total parameters, Qwen4-Max activates only 71 billion per token—25% fewer activated parameters compared to Qwen3.8-Max at the same 2.4T scale—delivering stronger capabilities at a lower inference cost.
Qwen4-Max is available now on QwenCloud via the Token Plan and API.

Kimi K3 tops AI benchmark in a first for Chinese models
Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 reached first place on Arena.ai's Frontend Code leaderboard on July 16, scoring 1,679 points, ahead of Claude Fable 5 (1,631) and GPT-5.6 Sol (1,618).
While the new ranking is still largely populated by Anthropic's Claude models, Kimi K3’s predecessor had ranked 18th on the same leaderboard, so the new model represents a mighty position improvement in just a single generation.
Kimi K3 is a 2.8-trillion-parameter MoE with a million-token context window and a new hybrid linear-attention mechanism called Kimi Delta Attention, designed predominantly for efficiency, which is typical for open-source models by Chinese firms that don't have access to all the GPU power that their Western counterparts do.
Moonshot has said the model's weights are expected to be released under a modified MIT license by July 27, which would make local deployment possible in addition to API access.
Kimi K3 vs Claude vs ChatGPT pricing
The new K3 AI model costs $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens through Moonshot's API, with a discounted $0.30 rate for cached input tokens during long chat thread sessions.

We’ve updated how the Bash Recovery score is calculated on the Agent Arena signal leaderboard and are now naming this signal, Bash Reliability.
There are two changes: how we detect bash failures, and how we turn them into a score.
- Detecting failures.
Previously, we used a simple set of rules to decide whether a bash call failed because of the agent’s mistake.
The previous rules sometimes misjudged which bash calls were real failures, flagging correct tests and empty searches; sometimes missing errors were hidden by piped commands.
We now use an LLM judge that looks at each call’s purpose, outcome, and cause of any error, and whether or not the error was fixed within the call.
This results in a more accurate assessment of whether a bash call failed.

polymarket-4664724.text:
OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra, its new frontier model “for your hardest projects”, and the lighter GPT-6.2 Sol on 17 November 2026.
Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users get both in ChatGPT Work and Codex; developers get them through the API.
The line that stands out in the system card is about safety.
OpenAI writes that Astra is “the first model we are deploying externally that meets the High threshold for AI Self-Improvement”.
Sol stays below it.
What High and Critical mean
Both ratings are OpenAI’s own, set under its Preparedness Framework.
A High rating for self-improvement, the company says, means the model’s impact is “equivalent to giving every OpenAI researcher an additional, highly capable research engineer as an assistant, relative to their 2024 baseline”.
On launch day it reworded the card to call this threshold “an early milestone for proactively preparing safeguards” for models that may one day improve themselves fully automatically.
Critical for cybersecurity means, by the card’s definition, that a model can develop working zero-day exploits in many hardened critical systems without human help, or plan and run a new kind of attack from a high-level goal alone.
Both GPT-6.2 models meet it, as GPT-6 Astra did in September (Quartz).
OpenAI says it tightened limits on higher-risk security help and built Control Room, a system that can halt a model’s output.
The card also records a regression: both models more often left out obstacles that blocked their work, such as a missing file.
OpenAI is investigating.
Price and the first outside test
- Astra in the API
- $8 input, $40 output per million tokens
- Change against GPT-6 Astra
- 20% cheaper
On Agents’ Last Exam, a test of multistep professional work, OpenAI reports Astra 5.2 points above GPT-6 Astra at under a third of the cost, and 5.5 points above Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 at 5% of the cost.
Epoch AI, a research group, graded six models by hand on tasks from its own work and published the results the same day.
Astra roughly tied that rival for a record on the Epoch Capabilities Index but averaged 65% on the realistic tasks, 17 points lower.
No model met Epoch’s standard for its own staff on any task.
Epoch found Astra too cautious in a data centre analysis and noted cleaner writing and graphic design than in GPT-6 Astra.
What comes next
This is the first Astra upgrade since OpenAI cancelled the release of GPT-6.1 Astra in September (The Next Web).
OpenAI says it will work to bring the GPT-6.2 models to Daybreak, its programme for security defenders.

polymarket-4664724.text:
Today, we’re excited to introduce Muse Spark 1.1, the latest model from Meta Superintelligence Labs and a significant upgrade from Muse Spark.
Muse Spark 1.1 is a multimodal reasoning model built for agentic tasks, with major gains in tool and computer use, coding, and multimodal understanding.
With these improvements, Muse Spark 1.1 advances the performance-efficiency frontier.
Together with this week’s launch of Muse Image, this release brings us closer to our vision of personal superintelligence: models that help you pursue your goals, create what you imagine, deepen your relationships, and take action on what you value most.
Along with this release, we are launching a public preview of the new Meta Model API where developers can access Muse Spark 1.1.
The model is available now in "Thinking" mode in the Meta AI app and on meta.ai.
Evaluations
For more details about our evaluations, see our report.
Agents
Muse Spark 1.1 delivers exceptional performance in personal agentic tasks that require planning and orchestration across a range of external apps and services.
It zero-shot generalizes to new native tools, MCP servers, and custom skills.
It tackles complex projects significantly faster than Muse Spark, as it is trained to orchestrate multi-agent systems to optimize end-to-end latency.
As the main agent, it can gather context, make a plan, and delegate execution across parallel subagents.
As a subagent, it adheres to its job, understands available tools, and knows when to escalate back to the main agent.
Muse Spark 1.1 can actively manage its context window of 1 million tokens.
It remembers actions, retrieves information from much earlier work, and compacts in a way that keeps the critical steps needed for later work.
Computer Use
Muse Spark 1.1 excels at computer-use workflows that unfold across multiple applications with information changing on-the-fly.
It maintains context across extended sessions, adapts to evolving requirements, and navigates unfamiliar interfaces with minimal human intervention.
Rather than reasoning through every desktop step one click at a time, Muse Spark 1.1 understands when to automate and when to use the interface directly.
We trained the model to write scripts when automation is faster, click when direct interaction is simpler, and generate batches of actions at each step.
Agentic dinner party organization: In real-world applications, new context arises that changes the task.
Muse Spark 1.1 notices these changes when placing the dinner order and makes necessary updates without user intervention.
Coding
Coding performance for Muse Spark 1.1 improved substantially on real-world tasks involving large, complex codebases.
It can diagnose and fix complex bugs, implement new features in enterprise-grade systems, and execute large code migrations.
In use cases like creating web applications and end-to-end question answering, Muse Spark 1.1 shows large gains over our first model.
We trained our model to smoothly adapt to diverse harnesses and reliably handle complex multi-turn dynamics.
Muse Spark 1.1 performs well with popular agentic coding setups, supporting common features like planning mode, goal conditioning, subagent delegation, and context compaction.
Debugging demo in OpenCode: Muse Spark 1.1 builds a chat web app, takes automated screenshots to identify user-visible failures, traces issues back to relevant code to implement fixes, and validates these changes.
The model seamlessly combines coding, multimodal understanding, and tool calling.
Across Meta, developers and researchers are using Muse Spark 1.1 daily to build faster and work smarter.
On our primary internal coding evaluation, Meta Internal Coding Bench, Muse Spark 1.1 significantly improves upon Muse Spark and is competitive with leading alternatives.
Researchers are now also automating model development and evaluation tasks by leveraging Muse Spark 1.1 in their workflows.
DeepSWE evaluation in OpenCode: Muse Spark 1.1 evaluates itself on a subset of DeepSWE tasks across different reasoning strengths and produces an analysis dashboard based on the results.
Multimodal
Along with coding and agentic capabilities, Muse Spark 1.1 excels in perception, multimodal reasoning, and tool use.
It can interact with real environments and produce grounded outputs with strengths in visual-to-code artifact generation, ultra-descriptive image and video captioning, and agentic workflow execution for multimodal use cases.
Muse Spark 1.1’s multimodal capabilities are especially valuable when perception and action need to happen together.
The model can inspect visual and audio, preserve details across a long workflow, and use those details while operating computers on the user’s behalf.
Facebook Marketplace agent: Using video shot from a smartphone, Muse Spark 1.1 extracts useful photos and reasons about the product to operate a user's browser and make a Facebook Marketplace listing on the user's behalf.
Safety
We conducted extensive safety evaluations before deployment, following the Advanced AI Scaling Framework, which defines evaluations, threat models, and deployment thresholds for our most advanced models.
Across all frontier risk categories — Chemical & Biological, Cybersecurity, and Loss of Control — our evaluations show Muse Spark 1.1 operates within safe margins.
Muse Spark 1.1 demonstrates strong resistance to direct jailbreaks and indirect attacks from untrusted data, prompt injection, and developer-prompt attacks.
Consequently, it shows better adversarial robustness, lower hallucination rates, and reduced sycophancy.
Our full safety posture for 1.1 is documented in our Muse Spark 1.1 Evaluation Report.
Availability
For the first time, developers can begin building with Muse Spark 1.1 via the new Meta Model API, now in public preview.
Early partners of Muse Spark 1.1 praise the model as a complete agentic foundation, pairing long context handling with strong coding and reasoning capabilities to handle large-scale agentic workloads.
“What’s most impressive about Muse Spark is how much it packs into one model: massive million-token context, full multimodal support (images, video, PDFs), built-in search with citations, strong reasoning, top-tier coding abilities (particularly frontend and design), structured output, and parallel tool calling — all in a clean OpenAI-compatible package.
A complete agentic foundation."
— Amjad Masad, CEO of Replit
“Meta is clearly building for serious agentic coding – strong tool use at a price point that makes it viable to run real coding workloads at scale.
That combination is rare, and it’s exactly why we wanted Cline developers to have access early.”
— Saoud Rizwan, CEO of Cline
“When tested against Box’s enterprise work evaluation set, Muse Spark delivered enterprise capabilities competitive with today's leading frontier models.
That level of intelligence, combined with its strengths in structured, procedural workflows across industries such as professional services, public sector, and industrial operations, makes it a compelling choice for organizations.”
— Yashodha Bhavnani, VP of AI Products at Box
"Muse Spark 1.1 is an awesome model for running agents.
Fast, powerful, and fun with OpenClaw.”
— Dave Morin, OpenClaw Foundation
We're thrilled to be releasing Muse Spark 1.1, a testament to our research momentum.
We have even more capable models in training and look forward to sharing what’s to come.
polymarket-4664724.title: Introducing Muse Spark 1.1

A weekend of deadly Houthi attacks has kept Riyadh's main airport closed through Oct.
17 and prompted airlines to extend flight suspensions, delivering another setback to Saudi Arabia’s ambitions to become a global aviation hub.
Saturday’s strike, which killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, was the deadliest attack in the kingdom in more than a decade.
The kingdom has spent recent years pouring billions into a new airline and airport infrastructure projects as part of a bid to compete with established Gulf rivals and position Riyadh as a global aviation hub.
Aerial attacks by the Yemeni militants have exposed just how vulnerable those ambitions are, as the US-Iran conflict continues to disrupt one of the world’s key corridors for international air travel.
What happened: A Notice to Airmen published on Flightradar24 said King Khalid International Airport would remain closed through Oct.
17 for precautionary reasons.
Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) separately confirmed that the suspension would continue while safety and operational checks were being completed, without specifying a reopening date.
The airport has been closed since Saturday’s attack.
Another strike on Sunday killed one person and injured 11.
The weekend attacks followed two strikes on Oct.
8 that killed three Saudi citizens and damaged a Saudia aircraft on the ground.

The Saudi-led coalition reported the interception of 8 Houthis UAVs and 3 ballistic missiles launched at Riyadh.[2] According to Reuters: "Two loud explosions were heard in Riyadh and smoke billowed into the sky", but "there was no sign of damage to the side of the defense ministry building that is visible from the main road or to any surrounding buildings.
The area was quiet on Tuesday evening, with normal traffic flows and no additional security measures.[2]
According to Saudi-led coalition spokesman Col.
Turki al-Malki, the Houthi attack was "a deliberate hostile action designed to target civilians".[2]

In March 2018, Houthi forces targeted Riyadh with missile attacks.
Reuters reported that Saudi forces said they shot down three missiles over Riyadh shortly before midnight.
Debris fell on a home in the capital, killing an Egyptian man and wounding two others.[3]
In June 2019, the Houthis launched cruise missiles at Abha International Airport and killed a Syrian civilian and wounded 47 others.[4][5][6][7]

Saudi-led coalition intercepts suspected Houthi missiles and drones
Fighting escalates in Yemen’s Marib and al-Jawf, as UN migration agency says more than 340,000 Yemenis displaced since August.
Saudi-led coalition forces fighting Yemen’s Houthis have said they intercepted two missiles and five drones targeting different parts of the country, allegedly launched by the Iran-backed rebel group.
“Air defences intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi terrorist militia towards Riyadh,” Turki al-Maliki, the Saudi-led coalition spokesperson, said in a post on X early on Sunday.

- list 3 of 3Siege fuels disease fears in Yemen’s Taiz
He said the coalition forces also shot down three drones in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern region on Sunday.
Earlier on Saturday, al-Maliki said two suspected Houthi drones “were intercepted and destroyed” in the Riyadh and southern regions.
Meanwhile, the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), claimed to have shot down an armed Saudi coalition reconnaissance aircraft carrying out “hostile operations in the airspace of al-Jawf”.
In a post on X, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the Iran-aligned group was able to “repel a number of Saudi military formations using several Yemeni-made surface-to-air missiles” and that it was the fifth aircraft the Houthis had shot down since the escalation began.
At least 26 people have been killed in suspected Houthi drone and missile attacks in Saudi Arabia since September 23, according to the kingdom’s authorities.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport, as well as the East-West pipeline and oil infrastructure in eastern and southern Saudi Arabia.
The interceptions come as the Saudi-led forces supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government also said they intercepted several drones launched towards the Yemeni city of Marib.
Yemeni army spokesman Colonel Majid al-Nuzaili said government forces had made gains against the Houthis during heavy fighting in the al-Hazm and Madghal districts of al-Jawf, as fighting intensified in Marib.
Al-Nuzaili said 321 Houthi leaders had been killed or wounded in 723 targeted operations by Saudi-backed forces in the Taiz, Lahij, Marib and al-Jawf governorates, and that 117 military vehicles used by the Iran-allied rebel group had been destroyed.
The coalition carried out at least 37 air strikes and 56 drone attacks, as well as 541 artillery strikes.
Houthi spokesman Saree said the Saudi-led coalition had launched 72 air strikes against the Houthis in the Saada, Taiz, Lahij and al-Jawf governorates over the past 24 hours.
He said the Houthis targeted Yemen’s Saudi-backed forces in the Kharaz area of the Lahij governorate with ballistic missiles.
Media outlets affiliated with the Houthis reported that two women and two children were injured as a result of artillery shelling by Saudi-backed forces in a residential neighbourhood of the Shuaub district in Sanaa, Yemen’s capital controlled by the Houthis.
More than 340,000 people have been displaced as a result of fighting in Yemen since August, according to the International Organization for Migration.
Security alert
As the fight between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis escalated, the US Embassy in Riyadh issued a nationwide security alert on Saturday urging Americans in the kingdom to exercise “heightened vigilance”, citing an increased threat of Houthi attacks.
The embassy said Houthi attacks on airports and other critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia had “caused civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions”, warning that hostilities could spread “rapidly”.
“Please take extreme caution if you choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia,” it said.

Coalition destroys 60 Houthi military targets in Yemen, intercepts cruise missile targeting Riyadh
RIYADH — The Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen has destroyed 60 Houthi military targets across four Yemeni governorates and intercepted a cruise missile launched toward Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh region.
Coalition spokesperson Maj.
Gen.
Turki Al-Malki said the targeted operation, announced early Wednesday morning, aimed to weaken the Houthi militia’s ballistic missile and drone capabilities and neutralize maritime threats.
Al-Malki said the operation targeted military sites across Sanaa, Al-Hudaydah, Amran and Saada governorates.
The operation included the destruction of tunnels used to store ballistic missiles in mountainous areas, along with workshops used to assemble and store drones, according to the Coalition.
Later Wednesday morning, the Coalition separately announced that it had intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the Houthi militia toward Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh region.

polymarket-5636955.text:
Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper hit in Houthi strike on Saudi wealth fund HQ
By Timour Azhari and Eman Abouhassira
RIYADH, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, headquarters of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, was struck on Thursday in a Houthi attack in the latest blow to the kingdom in its war with the Iran-backed Yemeni group.
Saudi Arabia's civil defence said a Houthi attack on a tower in Riyadh's financial centre caused material damage to several floors of the building and nearby buildings, but no injuries were reported, state news agency SPA said.
The statement did not identify the tower, but an accompanying photograph published by SPA showed the PIF Tower.
The Houthis said they had targeted Riyadh's financial centre twice on Thursday, first at dawn and again in the evening.
They also said they had attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Khamis Mushait airbase in southern Saudi Arabia and SADAF Petrochemical Company in Jubail in the kingdom's Eastern Province.
There was no immediate Saudi confirmation of these attacks.
The kingdom's foreign ministry said it reserved the right to take "all necessary measures" to defend its sovereignty and protect its citizens and national assets following the Houthi attack.
The strike blew out windows across seven to eight floors of the PIF Tower, bending parts of its metal facade.
It was the second time in less than two weeks that a Houthi attack damaged a landmark in Riyadh's financial district, with state oil company Aramco's building hit in a November 8 attack.
The King Abdullah Financial District was closed to visitors following the attack.
Three sources familiar with the matter said the building had been struck by an incoming Houthi missile.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had "dealt with a missile threat" launched towards Riyadh and that debris had fallen.
PIF, which stands for the Public Investment Fund, acknowledged receiving a Reuters request for comment.
The Houthis issued no immediate statement on the strike.
The Houthis have been firing at Saudi airports and oil infrastructure since Yemen's frozen civil war reignited in July amid the US-Iran war.
On the ground in Yemen, the group has seized swathes of territory from the Saudi-backed government, forcing it to stage a major retreat at the weekend.
Residents of the Saudi capital were awoken by a loud boom in the early hours of Thursday.
Saudi Arabia's civil defence issued several warnings of potential danger in Riyadh throughout Thursday, including after the attack, before announcing that the threat had passed.
The Houthi-run Saba news agency reported that Saudi aircraft had carried out airstrikes on the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital Sanaa early on Thursday, without providing further details.
Saudi authorities did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the strikes.
SAUDI SEES CAMPAIGN STRETCHING WELL INTO 2027
The conflict has dealt a blow to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's plans to develop and diversify the economy of Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil exporter and a US ally.
The prince met US Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper in Riyadh on Wednesday, Cooper's third publicly reported visit to Saudi Arabia since the Yemen conflict resumed.
Reuters reported on Wednesday that Saudi officials now foresee the campaign stretching on for up to six months, according to two Western officials briefed by the Saudis on the kingdom's plans.
A third source familiar with the Saudi plans confirmed the accounts.
The sources said the Saudis, who replaced the commander of their coalition fighting in Yemen this week, want to see their allies make gains on the ground before they enter any negotiations with the Houthis.
Meanwhile, the situation in Yemen has appeared to favour the Houthis, who have seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coast including the strategically vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait at its mouth, and have surrounded the city of Taiz in highlands overlooking the government's temporary capital Aden.
In the wider war, which began in February when the United States and Israel attacked Iran, there has been no sign of a breakthrough in negotiations mediated by Qatar.
Meanwhile, there has been an uptick in hostilities in the Gulf in recent days, with Iran firing at US allies Bahrain and Kuwait and US airstrikes hitting Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday.
Saudi Arabia first entered the Yemen conflict in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to try to restore Yemen's government to power after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and much of the country.
They fought to a bloody stalemate and in 2022 reached a ceasefire that lasted until summer this year.
(Reporting by Timour Azhari in Riyadh, Eman Abouhassira in Dubai, Enas Alashray and Ahmed Tolba and Yomna Ehab in Cairo; Writing by Nayera Abdallah and Tom Perry; Editing by Peter Graff and Alistair Bell)

Yemen’s Houthis renew strikes on Saudi Arabia as UNSC extends sanctions
Saudi-led coalition intercepts flurry of suspected Houthi missiles, drones targeting oil, military infrastructure.
Saudi-led coalition forces have said they intercepted suspected Houthi drones over Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh region and Eastern Province, as the UN Security Council agreed to extend sanctions on the Iran-allied group.
Major General Turki al-Maliki, the spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition, announced the interceptions of suspected Houthi drones on Thursday, in a statement carried by the Saudi Press Agency.

- list 2 of 3Saudi Arabia downs missiles fired at Riyadh after Houthi attack on pipeline
- list 3 of 3Yemeni forces, Houthis exchange attacks, claim to inflict heavy losses
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had targeted oil infrastructure and military assets in the kingdom, including a pumping station on the East-West Pipeline with a drone as well as the Yanbu oil facility on the Red Sea.
Riyadh says it has rerouted about 4 million barrels of crude per day via its East-West Pipeline to Yanbu, equivalent to about 4 percent of global supply.
Saree further claimed a military cargo plane at Sharurah airport close to Yemen’s border was targeted with a drone, while a ballistic missile launched towards Khamis Mushait airbase “scored a direct hit”.
The Houthi spokesperson added that their forces had targeted the Saudi Aramco headquarters in the capital, Riyadh, but rejected as a “grave falsehood” a Saudi assertion that the group had targeted the kingdom’s Mecca region on Wednesday.
Saudi-backed coalition forces fighting on behalf of Yemen’s internationally recognised government say they continue to confront the Houthis across all frontlines, targeting leaders, vehicles, reinforcements, weapons and positions.
Yemen’s Defence Ministry, citing the Saudi-backed Presidential Leadership Council, said the battle against the Houthis was moving towards its “desired objectives”, according to Yemen’s official pro-government Saba news agency.
A meeting convened by the Defence Ministry was held in the Marib governorate to discuss the ongoing operations against the Houthis, where ways to enhance coordination and integration between various military units that are part of the Dawn of Yemen offensive were also discussed.
Security Council extends sanctions
On Thursday, the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) unanimously voted in favour of extending sanctions related to Yemen for one more year, including freezing assets and enforcing travel bans, while demanding an end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
The mandate for the UN Panel of Experts on Yemen, which made the recommendations, was also extended.
UNSC members called on “all parties to refrain from escalatory actions and to resolve differences and disputes through negotiation”, while also backing the territorial integrity of both Saudi Arabia and Yemen.
“The resolution condemns the military escalation by the Houthis, their maritime and cross-border attacks against Saudi Arabia, and their threats to commercial shipping vessels,” the UNSC statement said.
The resolution emphasised that measures taken for the purpose of maintaining sanctions “shall not apply to humanitarian assistance or supplies for basic needs of civilians, without negatively affecting legitimate trade activities”.
“The council sanctions are merely a means, not an end in themselves,” said Ambassador Fu Cong, China’s envoy to the UN, who hoped that “the situation in Yemen will de-escalate as soon as possible”.
333,000 displaced
On Thursday, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said more than 333,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since the beginning of August, including more than 24,000 displaced in the past week.
Civilians “continue to pay a heavy price as violence damages health facilities, forces families from their homes, and hinders the work of humanitarians”, OCHA said.
Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia is pressing the European Union to adopt an EU Parliament resolution to designate the Ansar Allah Houthi movement as a “terrorist organisation”, according to the Reuters news agency, citing sources familiar with the drive.
But European officials told Reuters the bloc is concerned this could undermine a future peace process.
EU foreign policy spokesperson Anouar El-Anouni said the bloc was in regular contact with Riyadh on regional developments, but declined to comment on any specific discussions under way, according to Reuters.

Saudis say Riyadh airport partly reopens despite renewed Houthi threats
Saudi Arabia said its main airport resumed operations at two terminals on Sunday even as Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis vowed to keep striking the facility, which they called a “military target”.
King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had halted operations on October 10 following an attack claimed by the Houthis that killed 13 people, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.
Saudi Arabia said it intercepted another wave of missiles and drones on Sunday as fighting with the militant group continued unabated.
The Houthis said they had launched attacks on the air hub among other sites in the kingdom, including in Khamis Mushait and Jazan.
It was not immediately clear if those were the strikes the kingdom said it had blocked.
The conflict has become an increasingly destabilising element in the US-Israeli offensive against Iran, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in the wider war.

After Saudi authorities announced the partial resumption of operations at the airport, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree vowed the facility would “never be safe” and urged airlines, airport staff and travellers not to use it.
Late on Saturday, the airport said Terminal 1 would be designated for domestic flights and Terminal 2 for international flights operated by national carriers starting Sunday.
Despite the announcement, flight tracking data from Flightradar24 showed little traffic at the airport on Sunday.
The Saudi-led coalition said earlier this month that the Houthis had carried out 20 attacks on the airport between October 1 and 11.
Missile and drone attacks continue
Saudi civil defense said on Sunday that shrapnel from the interception of two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis over Khamis Mushait and Ahad Rafidah injured two people and damaged residential buildings and vehicles.
Civil defense authorities earlier issued emergency alerts for Riyadh and the cities of Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran on Sunday, before saying minutes later that the danger had passed.
The coalition said two drones and a ballistic missile were launched towards Riyadh, and a cruise missile towards the southern city of Khamis Mushait.
It later said it intercepted 10 ballistic missiles fired towards southern Saudi Arabia.
The Houthis said they attacked the airport and Saudi oil facilities on Saturday.
Saudi authorities did not comment directly on the Houthi statements.
Saudi Arabia has stepped up its strikes against the Houthis after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month, closing in on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait – a global maritime chokepoint and shipping route for Gulf oil producers on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula to the Strait of Hormuz.
The renewed fighting in Yemen has shattered a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022.
Saudi Arabia intervened in Yemen’s civil war in 2015 at the head of a coalition supporting the internationally recognised government, after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa a year earlier.

Exclusive-Covert Russian network exploited French riots on social media, EU report says
By Antoni Slodkowski and John Irish
NEW YORK/PARIS, Nov 9 (Reuters) - A covert Russian network sought to exploit last month's riots in France by using social media to blame the unrest on uncontrolled immigration and portray the government as having lost control, according to an internal EU assessment seen by Reuters.
A separate internal assessment, compiled by France's foreign ministry and also seen by Reuters, found that social media accounts linked to Israel and to the US MAGA movement also pushed "hostile narratives" around the riots, linking them to radical Islamism and migration.
Taken together, the assessments offer an insight into how external actors have been trying to use France's domestic turmoil for their own political ends, according to analysis by European disinformation specialists.
The European Union analysis found that a covert Russian network known as "Operation Overload" spread videos impersonating Western media outlets to target French audiences, some falsely claiming migrants had raped protesters or terrorist attacks were imminent.
The Russian foreign ministry did not respond to a request for comment.
In August, ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova rejected allegations by a French state watchdog agency of spreading disinformation about France's 2027 elections and said they would "not be the last concoction which the authorities will use to manipulate public opinion".
Rioting erupted in cities across France last month as demonstrations against rising living costs and declining public services spiralled out of control in some of the worst violence the country has witnessed for decades.
The EU analysis, which covers the period from October 7 to 21, found that Russia sought to "depict the French leadership as weak and increasingly authoritarian".
“Such events offer opportunities to undermine national governments, fuel fear and division, and shape public perceptions ahead of elections,” said the restricted-circulation EU document, prepared by disinformation experts in the bloc's diplomatic service.
It found no evidence that Moscow or other actors had instigated or escalated the protests, describing the activity as "the opportunistic exploitation of unrest".
POSTS BY RUSSIAN, ISRAELI ANDMAGA ACCOUNTS GOT MILLIONS OF VIEWS
The French foreign ministry's assessment found that the 10 most-viewed X posts on the unrest from "pro-Russian spheres" got 2.8 million views from October 16 to 18.
But those figures were dwarfed by the views achieved by X posts on the riots from accounts linked to the MAGA movement and to Israeli officials and influencers.
The 10 most-viewed X posts on France's unrest by MAGA-linked officials, media outlets and influencers got more than 49 million views from October 16 to 18, according to the French ministry report.
The 10 most-viewed posts from Israeli officials, government accounts, media outlets andinfluencers got more than 35 million views in the same period, the French report said.
CAMPAIGNS ARE PART OF 'NARRATIVE COMPETITION', EXPERT SAYS
Elina Treyger, a senior political scientist at the RAND Corporation think tank, said such campaigns wage a slow-burning "narrative competition" that over time can shape how Western democracies are seen in Europe and beyond.

It has a set of prices generated across three market layers that arbitrage keeps aligned.
The London OTC market is the largest layer by notional, with bilateral trades that capture physical demand, regional premiums and institutional accumulation.
COMEX futures (CME Group) is the speed layer: standardised 100-ounce contracts, mostly cash-settled, and typically the quickest venue to react to rate decisions and geopolitical shocks.

How the Gold Spot Price Works
The spot price is the market price for one troy ounce of gold for immediate delivery, quoted in U.S.
dollars.
It is derived from the most actively traded gold futures contract together with over-the-counter dealing, and it moves nearly around the clock as trading follows the sun from New York to London, Zurich, Shanghai and Hong Kong.
A troy ounce is 31.1034768 grams — about 10% heavier than the avoirdupois ounce used for groceries.
Physical bullion products trade at a premium above spot that covers fabrication and distribution; the premium is proportionally larger on small items than on large bars.
The chart above tracks this spot price.
The currency selector converts the same underlying quote into other currencies using live exchange rates.
Spot Price vs.
Futures Price
The spot price is for gold delivered now; a futures price is for gold delivered on a set date in the future, traded on exchanges such as COMEX.
The two normally differ by the cost of carrying gold to that date — storage, insurance and interest — which is why futures usually trade slightly above spot, a condition called contango.
When futures trade below spot — backwardation — it signals unusually strong demand for immediate physical delivery, and it’s rare enough in gold that it makes news when it happens.
The price on this page is the spot price; quotes you see for "gold futures" refer to the most active COMEX contract.
What Moves the Gold Price
Real interest rates and the Federal Reserve.
Gold pays no yield, so its strongest headwind is a high real (inflation-adjusted) interest rate — and its strongest tailwind is a falling one.
Fed rate decisions, inflation reports and Treasury yields are the events most likely to move the gold price on any given day.
Inflation and currency debasement.
Gold's reputation as an inflation hedge is best understood over long horizons: across decades, gold has broadly preserved purchasing power as paper currencies lost it, which is why demand rises when investors expect sustained inflation or growing government debt.
Over shorter periods the relationship is looser — in an inflation spike, what matters most is how the Fed responds, which is why real interest rates (above) are the better day-to-day guide.
The U.S.
dollar.
Gold is priced in dollars, so a weaker dollar tends to lift the gold price and a stronger dollar tends to weigh on it — even when nothing about gold itself has changed.
To see how much of a move is gold versus the dollar, the Kitco Global Index (KGX) tracks gold’s value measured against a basket of major currencies with the U.S.
dollar’s influence stripped out.
Central bank buying.
Central banks are among the largest holders of gold, and sustained official-sector purchases have been a major driver of demand in recent years.
Reserve announcements from major central banks regularly move the market.
Safe-haven and investment demand.
In periods of market stress, geopolitical risk or currency uncertainty, investors move into gold, lifting the price.
Flows into and out of gold-backed ETFs provide a visible, daily measure of this investment demand.
Gold Value by Purity — Karats and Fineness
Most gold isn't pure 24-karat bullion.
U.S.
jewelry is most commonly 14K gold, with 10K the legal minimum that can be sold as gold in the United States, while investment bars and coins such as the American Gold Eagle and Gold Buffalo are high-purity bullion (the Buffalo is .9999 fine).
Karat measures gold content out of 24 parts.
Each purity also has a fineness mark — the small number stamped on jewelry — which tells you exactly what an item contains:

So a ring marked 585 is 14-karat gold, and its gold content is worth 58.3% of the pure gold price by weight.
The Gold Value by Purity calculator on this page applies these percentages to the live spot price to estimate melt value — the value of the pure gold an item contains.
Melt value is not necessarily the price paid when buying or received when selling: dealers buying scrap typically pay below melt, and finished jewelry retails above it.
To value a specific item by its exact weight and purity, use the expanded gold calculator.
Gold Price History and All-Time High
Gold's current all-time high in U.S.
dollars is $5,589.38 per ounce, set on January 28, 2026.
Earlier landmarks put today's price in context: gold peaked near $850 in January 1980 during the inflation crisis, and at roughly $1,920 in September 2011 after the financial crisis.
Adjusted for inflation, the 1980 peak stood as the real record for decades — until January 2026, when gold surpassed it in real terms as well.
About Gold
Gold has been used as money and a store of value for more than five thousand years, and it neither rusts nor tarnishes — coins recovered after centuries underwater emerge with their surfaces intact.

Gold Spot Price Today
The gold spot price is the current market price for immediate delivery of one troy ounce of gold; traders often shorten it to spot gold.
Global commodity exchanges determine the spot price of gold today, with COMEX (part of CME Group) serving as the primary benchmark for price discovery.
The current gold spot price is quoted as XAU/USD, the price of one troy ounce in US dollars under the ISO 4217 currency code system.
This code reflects gold's unique status as both a commodity and a monetary asset.
Two interconnected markets drive gold pricing.
The London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) sets twice-daily benchmark fixes used to settle contracts and value portfolios worldwide.
COMEX futures in New York provide continuous electronic price discovery nearly 24 hours a day on weekdays.
The interaction between London's physical market and New York's futures market creates the global reference price that bullion dealers, jewelers, central banks, and ETF custodians all rely on.
The difference between spot and futures prices, known as the basis or contango, reflects storage costs, interest rates, and market expectations.
Futures trading at a significant premium to spot signals tightening physical supply or heightened forward demand.
Backwardation (spot above futures) is rare in gold and indicates acute physical shortages.
Gold's enduring value comes from its scarcity, durability, and millennia-long track record as a store of value.
Unlike fiat currencies, gold cannot be printed or debased by central bank policy.
Annual mine production adds roughly 1.7% to the existing above-ground supply of approximately 220,000 tonnes, giving gold one of the highest stock-to-flow ratios of any asset.
This fundamental scarcity, combined with gold's role as a safe-haven during periods of economic uncertainty, underpins its pricing dynamics across every major exchange.

(Kitco News) – Spot gold will trade on either side of $4,500 per ounce at the end of 2026, according to a new survey published by the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA).
The LBMA surveyed 16 professional analysts in July, and even as gold was trading at its 2026 lows, frequently dipping below $4,000 per ounce during the month, the average of the experts’ year-end price predictions was over 12% higher.
The highest year-end prediction from the survey’s respondents was $5,100 per ounce, representing a gain of an additional 15% from current prices, while the lowest forecast was $3,879, $100 below the 2026 low set in early July.
“The average price during [the first 7 month of 2026] was $4,595.75, some $135 below the average (for the whole year) predicted by 28 professional analysts polled by LBMA in January,” they noted.
“The mid-year pulse check provides an update to these figures and reveals that expectations have come into line with the reality of the first seven months.”
The LBMA said the projected full-year average gold price is now $4,604, with forecasted price highs during H2 2026 ranging from $4,872 to $5,800, and the lowest price forecast from respondents coming in at $3,450.
“The analysts’ list of drivers of the gold price - geopolitical issues notably in the Middle East, US inflation, the Federal Reserve’s direction of travel, central bank buying - has not materially altered since the beginning of the year although the emphasis has changed with greater attention being paid to the Fed under the new leadership of Kevin Warsh,” they wrote.

Gold fell to US$3,830.74 a troy ounce on November 16, 2026, its lowest level since October 2, 2025, as higher US government bond yields, a strong dollar and expectations of further interest rate rises weighed on prices.
Gold’s decline from January’s record of US$5,594.82 a troy ounce has reached 31.5%, according to Reuters analysis.
The metal is heading for its worst annual performance since 2015.
The US dollar has been trading near its strongest level since April 2025, making gold more expensive for buyers using other currencies and weakening demand in recent months.
Rising yields on US Treasury bonds have also reduced the appeal of gold, which pays no interest.
Markets expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by 25 basis points, or 0.25 percentage points, at its next meeting in December, with a smaller chance of a 50-basis-point increase, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool.
“Markets expect higher interest rates ahead, boosting the dollar and compounding gold’s headwinds, leaving it exposed to deeper declines,” said Nikos Tzabouras, senior financial editorial writer at FXCM.

CRUDE WRAP: WTI (F7) SETTLES USD 2.75 LOWER AT USD 83.26/BBL; BRENT (F7) SETTLES USD 1.19 LOWER AT USD 91.95/BBL
Newsquawk Staff ·
Oil saw losses as an unexpected crude build in the weekly metrics seemingly weighed, while Middle East updates offered little new.
In the weekly EIA data, crude stocks saw a surprise build and gasoline saw a greater-than-expected build, replicating what was seen in the private inventory metrics on Tuesday night.
Distillates also saw a larger-than-anticipated build.
Crude production rose 19k BPD W/W to 14.032mln BPD, with the SPR falling to 276.4mln bbls from 279.5mln bbls.
In the European morning, reports suggested that Iran's two-day peace proposal requires the US to end hostilities, lift oil sanctions and its naval blockade, and release frozen Iranian assets before Tehran reopens the Strait of Hormuz.
The reports added that the main disagreement concerns sequencing.
Elsewhere in the Middle East, benchmarks rose to session highs amid reports that Saudi Arabia expects its conflict with the Houthis to extend well into 2027.
The recent oil downside, which has seen WTI fall to lows not seen since late August, may also have been aided by a notable fall in the cost of shipping oil in the largest tankers since the start of November.
This reflects weaker demand for chartering and an unwinding of the geopolitical risk premium that sent shipping costs to a record high in October.
Freight rates for supertankers carrying oil from the Gulf of Oman to China are down 64% from their record high on October 8th.
Looking ahead, Fox News reported that US President Trump is set to meet Russian President Putin one-on-one at the APEC Summit on Thursday, November 19th.
For the record, WTI traded between USD [81.20]-[84.77]/bbl and Brent between USD [90.34]-[93.54]/bbl.
What it means
Sessions of this kind, where the official weekly stocks data confirms the private inventory survey from the prior evening, tend to extend rather than reverse the move, since the confirmation removes the excuse to fade the initial reaction.
The triple build across crude, gasoline and distillates points to the product side carrying as much weight as the headline crude number, a pattern that in past episodes of this kind has flagged softening refinery runs and demand rather than a one-off supply quirk.
The freight signal is the more informative tell: a large unwind in supertanker rates from record highs is the classic mechanism by which geopolitical risk premium bleeds out of the flat price, because the cost of moving barrels is where the Hormuz and sanctions premium is actually paid.
The Iran proposal, with disagreement centred on sequencing of sanctions relief against reopening the Strait, follows the established negotiating pattern in which headline risk stays two-sided until sequencing is resolved, and markets have historically sold the absence of escalation rather than buyin

quotes: WTI drops below $83.00 for the first time in nearly three months, more than 20% down from October highs.
polymarket-6172754.text:
WTI drops below $83.00 for the first time in nearly three months, more than 20% down from October highs.

Oil prices resumed their downtrend on Wednesday as an increase in US Crude inventories has calmed investors' fears of supply disruptions.
The price of the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) has dropped below $83.00 per barrel for the first time since late August, and is now more than 20% below October’s peak at the $104.00 area.
Weekly data released by the American Petroleum Institute released on Tuesday revealed that Oil inventories rose by 5.28 million barrels in the week ending on November 13, against expectations of a 0.5 million drawdown.
These figures follow another buildup of 9 million barrels in the previous week.
Tuesday’s data comes after Goldman Sachs warned on Monday about a severe Oil glut in 2027.
The investment bank sees Brent Crude trading at an average of $88 per barrel next year, and gradually declining to $78 by year-end as, according to its analysis, China will reduce its consumption by 400K barrels per day next year.
This has offset concerns of supply disruptions due to restrictions in Oil traffic through the key Strait of Hormuz, with the US-Iran conflict in a deadlock.
Hopes of a negotiated outcome have vanished after last week’s mediating attempts by Qatar failed, while attacks from Tehran on US allies in the region have intensified.
WTI Oil is a type of Crude Oil sold on international markets.
The WTI stands for West Texas Intermediate, one of three major types including Brent and Dubai Crude.
WTI is also referred to as “light” and “sweet” because of its relatively low gravity and sulfur content respectively.
It is considered a high quality Oil that is easily refined.
It is sourced in the United States and distributed via the Cushing hub, which is considered “The Pipeline Crossroads of the World”.
It is a benchmark for the Oil market and WTI price is frequently quoted in the media.
Like all assets, supply and demand are the key drivers of WTI Oil price.
As such, global growth can be a driver of increased demand and vice versa for weak global growth.
Political instability, wars, and sanctions can disrupt supply and impact prices.
The decisions of OPEC, a group of major Oil-producing countries, is another key driver of price.
The value of the US Dollar influences the price of WTI Crude Oil, since Oil is predominantly traded in US Dollars, thus a weaker US Dollar can make Oil more affordable and vice versa.
The weekly Oil inventory reports published by the American Petroleum Institute (API) and the Energy Information Agency (EIA) impact the price of WTI Oil.
Changes in inventories reflect fluctuating supply and demand.
If the data shows a drop in inventories it can indicate increased demand, pushing up Oil price.
Higher inventories can reflect increased supply, pushing down prices.
API’s report is published every Tuesday and EIA’s the day after.
Their results are usually similar, falling within 1% of each other 75% of the time.
The EIA data is considered more reliable, since it is a government agency.
OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) is a group of 12 Oil-producing nations who collectively decide production quotas for member countries at twice-yearly meetings.
Their decisions often impact WTI Oil prices.
When OPEC decides to lower quotas, it can tighten supply, pushing up Oil prices.
When OPEC increases production, it has the opposite effect.
OPEC+ refers to an expanded group that includes ten extra non-OPEC members, the most notable of which is Russia.

The next meeting will be held on 29 November 2026.

The seven OPEC+ countries, which previously announced additional voluntary adjustments in April and November 2023, namely Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman met virtually on 1 November 2026, to review global market conditions and outlook.
The seven participating countries decided to maintain September 2026 required production for December 2026 as detailed in the table below.
The seven countries reiterated their collective commitment to achieve full conformity with the Declaration of Cooperation.
The seven OPEC+ countries will continue to hold monthly meetings to review market conditions.
The next meeting will be held on 29 November 2026.

KABUL: Pakistan's government said on Monday that air strikes killed at least 28 militants in the Afghanistan-Pakistan border region, with one security official saying two Afghan provinces were targeted.
Hours earlier, Afghan Taliban officials accused Islamabad of killing at least three civilians in overnight air strikes on its territory.
The attacks broke nearly three months of relative calm.
Zabihullah Mujahid, chief spokesperson of the Taliban-run Afghan government, said the Afghan side "will respond appropriately to this aggression." A Pakistani official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the strikes happened in the Afghan provinces of Paktika and Kunar.
Pakistan's Information Ministry gave the death toll but its military did not immediately comment.
Relations between the former allies have been strained for years, with Islamabad accusing Kabul of harbouring militants who stage cross-border attacks.
Conflict escalated this February and hundreds died in air strikes, drone attacks, and artillery fire in the first half of the year.
Afghanistan's Taliban government denies harbouring anti-Pakistani insurgents and says militancy is Pakistan's internal problem.
The new air strikes came after a police facility in the northwestern Pakistani district of Kohat was attacked by militants on Friday, killing at least 24 people.
Prior militant attacks in Pakistan have often prompted retaliatory strikes from Pakistan.
A separate exchange of fire on Sunday killed six Pakistani soldiers and eight militants in the adjacent district of Hangu near the Afghan border, according to a Pakistani army statement.
At least one house in Kunar province was hit in the strikes on Monday, killing three members of the same family and injuring four others, Taliban deputy spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat said in a post on X.
In Paktika, two locations were bombed, destroying a shop and an unoccupied house, with no casualties, he added.
"Everyone was frightened," said Mula Khan, a 55-year-old resident who heard the strikes.
Pakistan's widening insurgencies are waged by competing groups with different support bases and ideologies but a common enemy in the Pakistani state.
Last week's attack in Kohat was claimed by a militant group.
At the time, that stood in stark contrast with Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and its insurgency against the Pakistani government in the northwest.
Bahadur's group turned against Pakistan after a major Pakistani military offensive around 2015 that targeted a safe haven of the group in North Waziristan district, Basit said.
That pushed the group's fighters into Afghanistan.
The long-term repercussions of that shift are still playing out today, said Basit, as Bahadur's group has become "an umbrella of different militant groups which are the architect and Gul Bahadur is the face." W
