Pakistan and Afghanistan agreed early on Friday morning to continue a ceasefire between the two countries following a rapid deterioration of ties and a brief conflict along their shared border earlier this month.
A second round of discussions between Pakistani and Afghan Taliban delegations had began in Istanbul on Saturday, but Islamabad’s long-standing concern over terror attacks emanating from Kabul remained a major point of contention, resulting in a stalemate.
A breakthrough came after Türkiye and Qatar salvaged the dialogue process for the second time in less than a week, following Pakistan’s announcement on Wednesday that the talks had “failed” and that its negotiators were preparing to return home.
A joint statement released by Türkiye, the host of the latest round of talks, early on Friday stated “further modalities of the implementation will be discussed and decided” during a principal-level meeting in Istanbul on November 6.
Though the statement didn’t specify who the “principals” would be, it is expected that it meant the defence ministers of the two countries, who led their sides in the first round in Doha, would now meet in Istanbul.
The joint statement further said that during this period, the two countries also agreed on a “monitoring and verification mechanism” to ensure the maintenance of peace and to impose a penalty on the side that breaches the ceasefire.
“All parties have agreed to put in place a monitoring and verification mechanism that will ensure maintenance of peace and to impose penalties on the violating party,” said the joint statement released by Türkiye’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The statement further said that as mediators, Türkiye and Qatar expressed their appreciation for the “active contribution of both parties” and the two countries will continue their cooperation with both sides for “lasting peace and stability”.
The same statement was also released by Qatar’s foreign ministry.
Türkiye and Qatar have deep ties with Pakistan, while Qatar also played a major role in the negotiations between the Afghan Taliban and Nato forces.
Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid, commenting on the development, said, “Just as the Islamic emirate seeks good relations with other neighbouring countries, it also desires positive ties with Pakistan and remains committed to relations based on mutual respect, non-interference in internal affairs and not posing a threat to any side.”
The joint statement came shortly after Defence Minister Khawaja Asif — who had earlier issued a strongly worded warning to Kabul after the stalemate in talks — said that a “ray of light” was visible in the Istanbul negotiations.
“Different drafts are being exchanged for an eventual agreement.
You can say that some ray of light is visible; there is very guarded optimism.
Let’s hope that some shape emerges from this,“ he stated while speaking on Geo News show ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Sath’.
“Qatar and Türkiye are very respected by us and are our well-wishers.
Türkiye clearly openly supported us in the Pakistan-India conflict, so we respect them and their opinion,” the defence minister said.
‘Verifiable action’
The Istanbul negotiations centred on Pakistan’s core demand that Afghanistan take “clear, verifiable and irreversible action” against the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and other terrorist groups involved in cross-border attacks from Afghan territory.
Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, speaking earlier in Peshawar, reiterated Pakistan’s red lines, saying that while Islamabad desired peace with all its neighbours, it “will not allow cross-border terrorism to be perpetrated from Afghan soil against Pakistan.”
The Taliban delegation, while participating in the dialogue, however, maintained that it could not fully control TTP operatives.
A senior Taliban official said the Afghan side had offered to detain and expel any TTP members found on Afghan territory.
“But Pakistan keeps insisting that we control TTP’s attacks inside Pakistan,” the official said.
“These fighters are Pakistani nationals operating within Pakistan.”
Pakistani negotiators also demanded that the Taliban formally declare the TTP a terrorist organisation and publicly denounce it as a fitna — an Islamic term for sedition or mischief.
Diplomatic sources said direct interaction between the two delegations remained limited throughout the five days, with most communication handled through mediators.
“Even during meal breaks, the sides barely spoke,” one source said.
Afghanistan continues to deny harbouring militants, accusing Pakistan instead of violating its sovereignty through airstrikes and, according to Afghan media, allowing US drones to operate from its airspace — a charge Islamabad denies.
Kabul insisted during the talks that any future agreement must include assurances against such operations.
While the Istanbul agreement marks a breakthrough after days of tension, diplomats cautioned that deep mistrust persists.
“This is a framework for peace, not yet peace itself,” a foreign diplomat said.
“It will take sustained verification, discipline and trust to make it hold.”
Border skirmishes and talks
Pakistan and Afghanistan saw a worsening of ties during recent weeks, which featured border skirmishes, counter-statements and allegations.
The hostilities began earlier this month when an attack was launched on Pakistan from Afghanistan on the night of October 11.
The attack had followed an allegation from the Afghan Taliban of airstrikes by Pakistan into Afghanistan — an accusation which Islamabad has neither confirmed nor denied.
For its part, Islamabad has long demanded that the Taliban stop terror groups from using its soil against Pakistan.
The Taliban, however, deny the allegation of allowing terrorists to operate from Afghan soil.
Meanwhile, Pakistan continues to grapple with the issue of terrorism and has suffered multiple casualties among security forces in intelligence-based operations.
After the initial skirmish on October 11, multiple others took place along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.
Meanwhile, strikes by Islamabad also targeted Gul Bahadur group camps in Afghanistan.
Eventually, the two sides came together for dialogue in Doha, which resulted in a temporary ceasefire, as well as a commitment to reconvene in Istanbul to work on mechanisms for lasting peace and stability between the two countries.
Last week, the second round of talks, which were being mediated by Türkiye and Qatar, between the two sides began in the Turkish capital.
But on Wednesday, Tarar announced in a post on X that the latest round of talks between Islamabad and Kabul in Istanbul “failed to bring about any workable solution”.
He also asserted that Pakistan would continue to take all possible measures to protect its citizens from terrorism.

ISLAMABAD – Pakistani and Afghan border forces exchanged fire at several points along their border on Sunday, as the military warned that the Afghan Taliban would not be able to withstand the “punishment” Islamabad could inflict if Kabul failed to rein in terrorists.

However, tensions remained high in the Angoor Adda area of Lower South Waziristan.

Border clashes
According to locals, gunfire erupted at Torkham on Sunday when Afghan authorities once again started construction on a disputed check post.
Authorities at Torkham said the Afghan side began work on the controversial Zangali check post, situated within a 100-metre radius of the Afghan side of the border, despite Pakistan’s strong objections.

The two nations had previously agreed to refrain from building security structures within a 100-metre radius of the border.

The meeting on 19 October brought together the foreign ministers of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan alongside Rubio.
In a joint statement issued after the meeting, the ministers said their governments attached particular importance to combating terrorism and transnational organised crime and strengthening border security.
However, despite repeated concerns from Central Asian countries about terrorist threats and the activities of extremist groups in Afghanistan, the joint statement from the Samarkand meeting made no direct reference to Afghanistan or the Taliban.
The statement said cooperation between the United States and Central Asian countries would be expanded to tackle illegal migration, human trafficking, drug trafficking and arms smuggling.
The two sides also emphasised stronger cybersecurity cooperation and efforts to counter digital threats and cybercrime.
Elsewhere in the statement, member countries stressed greater cooperation on nuclear security, the protection of nuclear materials and the peaceful use of nuclear energy.
Expanding Economic and Trade Cooperation
The joint statement said the United States and Central Asian countries would work together to expand trade and investment, strengthen transport connectivity and develop the Trans-Caspian trade route.
The cooperation is intended to increase bilateral and intra-regional trade, simplify customs procedures and promote a competitive market in Central Asia.
The two sides also emphasised expanding cooperation in energy, mineral extraction and processing, and developing high-value supply chains.
According to the statement, member countries aim to use their natural resources and technological capacity to support economic growth, increase exports and create new business opportunities.
Technology development, e-commerce, English-language education and greater digital connectivity were also identified as areas of cooperation between the United States and Central Asian countries.
Rubio Holds Bilateral Talks With Regional Foreign Ministers
Following his meetings with Central Asian foreign ministers, Rubio said cooperation between Washington and countries in the region could create new business opportunities, strengthen economies and contribute to greater regional security.
Rubio also said he held a separate meeting with Uzbekistan’s Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov.
According to Rubio, the two discussed expanding the strategic partnership between Washington and Tashkent, including cooperation on infrastructure, space technology, critical minerals and the C5+1 framework.
The US secretary of state also emphasised expanding bilateral economic and security cooperation during a meeting with Kazakhstan’s foreign minister.
He thanked Kazakhstan for supporting peace initiatives by the Donald Trump administration, including the Abraham Accords.
Sergio Gor, the US ambassador to India and special envoy for South and Central Asian affairs, said Rubio’s meetings with regional foreign ministers focused on Washington’s commitment to supporting the sovereignty of Central Asian countries, energy security and stronger supply-chain resilience.
What Is the C5+1 Mechanism?
The Samarkand meeting was held under the C5+1 mechanism, a framework established in 2015 between the United States and the five Central Asian countries of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Kyrgyzstan.
The mechanism aims to expand political, economic, trade, security and energy cooperation between the United States and countries in the region.
Afghanistan Absent From the Agenda
Afghanistan shares borders with Central Asian countries, and security developments there have contributed to regional concerns over terrorism and extremism.
Countries in the region have repeatedly expressed concern in recent years about the activities of Islamic State Khorasan Province and other armed groups in Afghanistan.
However, the joint statement from the Samarkand meeting did not identify Afghanistan as a specific area of cooperation or security concern.
Instead, it referred only to the members’ broader commitment to combating terrorism, transnational organised crime and cross-border threats.
The C5+1 framework was established in 2015 between the United States and five Central Asian countries to expand political, economic, security and energy cooperation between Washington and the region.

25 February, 20:50
Stock photo: Getty Images
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US President Donald Trump held a phone call on the evening of 25 February.
Source: Dmytro Lytvyn, Zelenskyy's communications adviser, speaking with journalists, as reported by European Pravda; Axios correspondent Barak Ravid on X (Twitter)
Details: Lytvyn said the call between Zelenskyy and Trump took place on Wednesday evening and had already ended by the time he confirmed it at about 20:40 Kyiv time.

Background:
- In an address marking the fourth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion, Zelenskyy stressed that it is important for the US president to visit Ukraine so that he can understand that pressure must be applied to Russia.
- He said Moscow is "playing" the US by pretending to engage in negotiations and has no real intention of ending the war.
- Zelenskyy has pointed out it is "not fair" that Trump continues to publicly call on Ukraine, rather than Russia, to make concessions for the sake of peace.

polymarket-6440135.text:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy had a phone call with President of the United States Donald Trump.
The Head of State congratulated the President of the United States on his birthday and wished him every success, above all in his work to end Russia’s war against Ukraine.
The leaders discussed many key issues in considerable detail, including peace.
The President of Ukraine also thanked the President of the United States for all the support America has been providing to Ukraine.
“We remember with gratitude every step of that support – from Javelins to Patriots,” Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.
The Presidents discussed things that could help bring about peace now.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy informed Donald Trump about the latest developments on the battlefield and how Ukraine’s position has strengthened.
The leaders agreed that they would discuss more during their meeting at the G7 Summit.
“We have some good ideas that could help advance peace and protect lives.
Thank you!” Volodymyr Zelenskyy emphasized.

Trump says he had "very good" call with Zelenskyy one day after speaking to Putin
Washington — President Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke on the phone Wednesday morning in a call that lasted roughly an hour, according to Mr.
Trump.
"Just completed a very good telephone call with President Zelenskyy of Ukraine," the president wrote on Truth Social.
"It lasted approximately one hour.
Much of the discussion was based on the call made yesterday with President Putin in order to align both Russia and Ukraine in terms of their requests and needs."

Trump said Putin agreed to a 30-day ceasefire against Ukraine's energy and infrastructure.
The commitment fell short of the full ceasefire pushed by the U.S.
and agreed to by Ukraine.

Trump "fully briefed" Zelenskyy on the call with Putin, and Mr.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he spoke with his US counterpart Donald Trump for a second consecutive day on Sunday, calling the conversation "very productive".

Zelenskyy has new call with Trump amid Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he spoke with his US counterpart Donald Trump for a second consecutive day on Sunday, calling the conversation "very productive".
The two leaders discussed a range of topics, which were agreed on a day prior, including defence, the use of long-range weapons such as the Tomahawk cruise missile, and Ukraine's energy sector.
Zelenskyy also urged Trump to broker peace in Ukraine, similarly to what he did in the Middle East, adding that Russia is currently taking advantage of the war in the region.
"Moscow allows itself to escalate its strikes, openly exploiting the fact that the world is focused on ensuring peace in the Middle East," Zelenskyy said.
"That is precisely why no weakening of pressure can be allowed.
Sanctions, tariffs, and joint actions against the buyers of Russian oil – those who finance this war – must all remain on the table," he added.
The phone calls come as Russia continues its campaign on Ukraine's energy infrastructure.
Overnight on Monday,Moscow targeted the Odesa region and its critical infrastructure, only a day after it struck energy facilities in the region, which resulted in blackouts in multiple towns.

'Security guarantees must be ironclad' — Zelensky speaks to Trump's envoys ahead of trilateral peace talks
President Volodymyr Zelensky held a phone call on Nov.
4 with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the U.S.
Special Envoys representing the White House in negotiations to end Russia's war against Ukraine.
The call comes ahead of the next round of trilateral peace talks, scheduled for Nov.
10 in Abu Dhabi.
Zelensky said he "had a very detailed conversation" with Witkoff and Kushner that lasted an hour and a half.
Among the primary topics were air defense munitions, the U.S.-Ukraine Drone Deal, and post-war security guarantees.
The Abu Dhabi talks will be held at the team level, with delegates from all three countries holding technical negotiations that could lead to a leader-level summit involving Zelensky, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and U.S.
President Donald Trump.
Both Zelensky and Putin expressed willingness to hold negotiations after meeting with Witkoff in Oslo and St.
Petersburg, respectively, in October.
"The pace of negotiations needs to be as intense as possible to end this war as quickly as possible," Zelensky said on Nov.
4.
"Ukraine is ready to take the necessary steps, our proposals are clear, and we have presented them to the American side."
U.S.
representatives also took part in talks with European partners in Brussels earlier in the day.
The negotiations were meant to coordinate joint peace efforts ahead of the Abu Dhabi meeting.
Kyiv has long called for a ceasefire along the current battle lines, while Moscow has repeatedly rejected truce proposals and demanded Ukraine cede unoccupied territory.
U.S.-brokered peace negotiations in Trump's second term have done little to move past this impasse.
Previous talks have yielded prisoner exchanges and some limited, short-term truces.

Trump announces plans to host 2026 G20 summit at his Doral resort
Washington — The United States plans to host the 2026 Group of 20 summit of world leaders at President Trump's golf course and spa in Doral, Florida, fulfilling a plan the president initially proposed during his first term.
Mr.
Trump revealed his decision to hold the G20 in Miami in the Oval Office at the White House on Friday.
National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett, who is seen as a potential future nominee to lead the U.S.
Federal Reserve, is set to serve as the point person for the summit.
The president said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is organizing the agenda for the meeting, which will focus on "unleashing economic prosperity by limiting, eliminating the burdens of regulations, unlocking affordable energy and pioneering new technologies."
The White House said in a statement Friday that Trump Doral would host the summit "at-cost, and will receive no profit from either the State Department or a foreign government." The gathering is scheduled for Dec.
14-15, 2026.
Mr.
Trump planned to host a G7 summit at the resort in 2020 but dropped the idea amid widespread criticism and ethical concerns about hosting a major global gathering at one of his own properties, which would reap revenue from the gathering.
Ultimately, the meeting was scrapped and held virtually as a result of the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.
The resort, which Mr.
Trump purchased in 2012 for $150 million, first opened in the 1960s.
Situated in a densely populated area of metro Miami, it sits beneath the flight approach route to Miami International Airport, and includes four golf courses, a 48,000-square-foot spa, a massive pool with a 125-foot slide, and a more than 24,000-square-foot ballroom.
Miami Mayor Francis Suarez was in the Oval Office for Mr.
Trump's announcement.
The G20 is an economic forum comprising 19 countries and two other blocs, the European Union and the African Union, representing most of the world's largest developed and emerging economies.
Member countries account for around 85% of global gross domestic product and more than 75% of global trade, according to the G20 website.
It is larger and more geographically diverse than the G7, which includes the U.S., Canada, Japan and other European powers.
The location of the meeting alternates among member nations, and this year's G20 will take place in November in South Africa, but Mr.
Trump has signaled he doesn't plan to attend, amid disagreements with the South African government over its treatment of White farmers.
Host nations may also invite other countries to attend as observers, and the president extended an invitation for next year's G20 summit to the newly elected president of Poland, Karol Nawrocki, when he was at the White House on Wednesday.
An administration official said the U.S.
"will be taking a back-to-basics approach to its host year, streamlining the summit and related workstreams and aligning the agenda with the G20's founding goals of economic growth and financial stability." As a result, the official said the White House expects "the guest list to be smaller than recent G20 summits."
polymarket-6440135.title: Trump announces plans to host 2026 G20 summit at his Doral resort

The 2026 G20 Doral Summit will be the twenty-first meeting of the Group of Twenty (G20), a meeting of heads of state and government planned from 14 to 15 December 2026.
It will be held at the Trump National Doral Miami, a property of the host, U.S.
president Donald Trump, in Doral, Florida.[1] The announcement was made by Miami Mayor Francis Suarez in the Oval Office and later confirmed by Doral Mayor Christi Fraga.
On 27 November 2025, President Trump announced that South Africa will not be invited to the 2026 G20 summit, citing its treatment of Afrikaners and a dispute over South Africa's refusal to transfer G20 hosting duties to a U.S.
Embassy representative at the end of the 2025 G20 Johannesburg summit.[2]
This will be Emmanuel Macron's last G20 summit, this will be Andy Burnham's first G20 summit, after winning the 2026 Labour Party leadership election in mid 2026 [3]

Bitcoin ETFs Break Outflow Streak Amid Market Decline
Bitcoin ETFs see first inflow after $1.91B outflow.
Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded their first capital inflow after seven trading sessions with a cumulative outflow of $1.91 billion.
However, this did not impact the price of the leading cryptocurrency: on November 17, the asset failed to hold above $65,000.
Over the weekend, Bitcoin dropped to around $62,100 — the lowest since July.
The asset has declined for six consecutive weeks.
The sell-off was accompanied by outflows from cryptocurrency funds, a drop in altcoins, and forced liquidation of trader positions worth billions of dollars.
Investors Withdraw $2.35 Billion from Bitcoin ETFs in Two Weeks
According to Farside Investors, from November 5 to 13, U.S.
spot Bitcoin ETFs lost capital for seven consecutive trading sessions, with a total outflow of $1.91 billion.
Over the two full weeks from November 2 to 13, investors withdrew approximately $2.35 billion.
In each of the five-day periods, losses exceeded $1 billion.
However, on November 16, the streak ended.
Funds attracted $7.9 million, with the majority coming from BlackRock’s IBIT — $76.5 million.
Meanwhile, GBTC lost $34.6 million, and FBTC lost $11.3 million.
Outflows Affect Ethereum and Other Crypto ETFs
The pressure also spread to other cryptocurrency investment products: during the week of November 9 to 13, U.S.
spot crypto ETFs collectively lost about $1.55 billion.
This amount includes outflows from Bitcoin funds — approximately $1.07 billion during the specified period.
Ethereum ETFs lost $398.9 million over the week.
The negative trend continued for the seventh consecutive week, with a total outflow during this period reaching approximately $2.42 billion.
Solana-based funds lost $32.1 million over the week, extending a similar streak to six weeks.
Products on Hyperliquid saw an additional $4.3 million withdrawn.
Among the 15 categories of U.S.
spot crypto ETFs tracked by SoSoValue, only Avalanche ended the week with an inflow of $227,000.
The Fear and Greed Index stood at 12 points, remaining in the extreme fear zone.
Liquidations Intensify Decline
Over the weekend of November 14–15, the cryptocurrency market experienced a massive wave of forced position liquidations.
According to Decrypt, during one 24-hour period, the volume of liquidations approached $2 billion.
According to CoinGlass, at the time of writing, the daily liquidation volume was $273.3 million.
Simultaneously, the total open interest in cryptocurrency futures increased by 3% to $111 billion, writes CoinDesk.
Why Bitcoin Hasn’t Recovered
The crypto market is simultaneously affected by expectations of tighter U.S.
monetary policy and a sell-off in tech stocks.
According to Reuters, investors are reassessing their stance on risk assets amid a strengthening dollar, high U.S.
government bond yields, and uncertainty surrounding the tech sector.
Nvidia is also drawing attention.
Its quarterly report is expected after the U.S.
market closes on November 17 — the first since Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO.
Earlier in November, analysts at Wintermute warned of the risk of Bitcoin falling below $60,000.
They linked the cautious forecast to expectations of a Fed rate hike, weakening demand, and a reduction in stablecoin supply.

Bitcoin ETFs lose $1 billion for the second week in a row as crypto funds, except one, continue bleeding
The 12 U.S.
spot bitcoin funds have lost $1.91 billion over seven straight trading days, and no other crypto ETF categories, save one, saw any net inflows last week.
Quick Take
- U.S.
spot bitcoin ETFs posted $1.07 billion in net outflows last week, their second consecutive week with over $1 billion in redemptions.
- The funds have seen outflows for seven straight trading days, a $1.91 billion run that is their longest since a 10-day streak in late June.
- U.S.
spot crypto ETFs lost about $1.55 billion combined, and Avalanche funds’ $227,000 was the only weekly inflow among the 15 categories SoSoValue tracks.
- Spot ether ETFs lost $398.9 million for a seventh straight negative week, one short of the category’s record, while Solana and Hyperliquid funds each extended their weekly outflow streaks to six, their longest since launch.
U.S.
spot bitcoin Bitcoin (BTC) ETFs saw $1.07 billion in net outflows last week, their second straight week with more than $1 billion leaving the funds, per The Block's analysis of SoSoValue data.
The last time the funds posted back-to-back $1 billion outflow weeks was in late May and early June.
The selling stretched to nearly every crypto ETF category.
Of the 15 groups of U.S.
spot crypto funds tracked by SoSoValue, 10 posted net outflows last week and four reported no flows at all.
Avalanche Avalanche (AVAX) funds were the only category with a weekly inflow, taking in a minute $227,000 on Thursday.
Overall, U.S.
spot crypto ETFs saw about $1.55 billion in total leave the funds.
The bitcoin funds saw outflows in all five days last week.
They lost $201.1 million on Monday, $95 million on Tuesday, $299.9 million on Wednesday, $284 million on Thursday and $185.5 million on Friday.
Combined with the $1.28 billion that left the funds the week before, bitcoin ETFs have now shed $2.35 billion over two weeks.
That is the largest two-week total since the fortnight ending June 5, when the funds lost $3.14 billion.
Bitcoin funds deepen 2026 losses with seven-day outflow streak
Friday's outflow was the bitcoin funds' seventh consecutive daily loss, a losing streak that has drained $1.91 billion from the funds since it began Nov.
5.
It is the longest daily outflow streak since the 10-session stretch from June 17 to July 1, which drained about $2.71 billion, as The Block reported at the time.
BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $143.5 million of Friday's outflows, or about 77% of the total, per SoSoValue.
Fidelity's FBTC lost $41.9 million, and the other 10 funds reported no flows.
IBIT currently holds bitcoin worth $53.99 billion against $64.19 billion in cumulative inflows since launch.
Bitcoin ETFs have come to lose $2.35 billion in November after nine trading days, already their largest monthly outflow since June, when $4.51 billion left the funds.
They are now down about $1.98 billion for 2026, more than double the $914.1 million deficit they carried a week earlier after flipping negative for the year.
The outflows came as bitcoin dropped below $69,000 early Friday, its lowest level since Aug.
20 at the time, as traders weighed Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO and expectations of another Federal Reserve rate hike, as The Block reported.
The world's most valuable cryptocurrency fell further on Saturday morning, currently trading around $65,650, per The Block's Bitcoin price page.
Ether funds approach record outflow streak
Spot ether Ethereum (ETH) ETFs lost $398.9 million last week, per SoSoValue, their seventh consecutive negative week; the category has twice posted eight-week outflow streaks, most recently when it matched that record in early July, so another negative week would tie it again.
The seven-week losing streak has pulled about $2.42 billion from the funds since late September, per SoSoValue's data.
Monday's $184.5 million outflow was last week's largest, followed by $144.8 million on Wednesday and $70.6 million on Thursday.
A minuscule $2.4 million inflow on Friday ended a six-trading-day outflow streak worth $594.4 million.
Fidelity's FETH drew $11.6 million that day, offsetting a $9.3 million outflow from Grayscale's Ethereum Mini Trust, while BlackRock's ETHA reported no flows.
Ether ETFs are now down about $804.5 million for 2026, nearly double the $405.6 million deficit from a week earlier.
Net assets fell 15.5% over the week to $10.85 billion, their lowest since Aug.
18 and about $670 million below the funds' $11.52 billion in cumulative net inflows.
Altcoin funds extend outflows, save for one
Spot Solana ETFs lost $32.1 million last week, per SoSoValue, their sixth straight negative week and the longest such run since the funds launched in October 2025.
The outflow streak began the same week the funds snapped a record 14-week inflow run, and it has drained $197.4 million since.
The Solana funds posted outflows in every session last week, extending their daily losing streak to seven days.
Fidelity's FSOL accounted for all of Friday's $3.1 million outflow.
Net assets fell to $1.14 billion from $1.31 billion a week earlier, though, unlike their BTC and ETH brethren, the funds remain about $644.1 million positive for the year.
Grayscale's Zcash fund, ZCSH, the only U.S.
spot Zcash ETF, lost $30.7 million, nearly as much as the nine Solana funds combined, per SoSoValue.
It was the fund's second straight negative week, and the outflow matched an early-October week as its largest since late September.
ZCSH's net assets fell 32% over the week to $523.7 million.
Spot XRP ETFs shed $19.1 million, per SoSoValue, their largest weekly outflow since mid-March and a second straight negative week.
Most of it left on Monday and Tuesday, at $10.4 million and $7.6 million, respectively.
On Friday, Grayscale's GXRP lost $5.5 million while Franklin's XRPZ took in $4.5 million.
The three U.S.
Hyperliquid ETFs lost $4.3 million, extending their weekly outflow streak to six, the longest since they began trading in May, per SoSoValue.
Smaller funds tracking NEAR, Chainlink, Hedera and Polkadot lost between $99,000 and $1.4 million each.
The BNB, Dogecoin, Tron and Litecoin funds reported no flows for the week.
The Avalanche funds’ modest $227,000 inflow on Thursday, their only day with any net flows, formed the only black in a sea of red last week.

Solana’s SOL token has fallen to its lowest levels since mid-August, trading near $75 in mid-November 2026.
The drop continues a multi-week slide that has erased roughly a quarter of its value over the past month and left the asset more than 70 percent below its January 2025 peak near $293.
Price action has tracked broader cryptocurrency weakness rather than any network-specific failure, with Bitcoin’s declines amplifying selling in higher-beta assets such as SOL.
Leveraged long positions were liquidated in waves as the wider market sold off, while large holders transferred substantial quantities of SOL onto exchanges, increasing near-term supply.
Sustained redemptions from Solana-linked exchange-traded products have removed a source of demand that had supported the token earlier in the year.
Institutional flows across major crypto ETFs have turned sharply negative.
Over the five trading days ending November 10, U.S.
spot crypto funds covering Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, Hyperliquid, and Zcash recorded combined net outflows of approximately $1.48 billion.
Bitcoin products absorbed the largest share at about $1.06 billion, while Ethereum funds lost $326 million; together they accounted for the bulk of the withdrawals.
Solana ETFs contributed roughly $47.4 million in redemptions, with XRP, Hyperliquid, and Zcash vehicles adding smaller amounts.
Bitcoin and Ethereum funds registered net inflows on only one session during the stretch, and Solana products have not recorded a single positive day since October 21.
Year-to-date through mid-November, Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs stand at a combined net outflow of roughly $2.25 billion, reversing earlier accumulation.
The pattern contrasts with renewed buying in traditional equity ETFs after an early-November equity selloff, underscoring a temporary divergence in risk appetite.Regulatory developments in China have added another headwind.
An unnamed official at the People’s Bank of China told the central-bank-supervised Financial News that authorities had halted planned offline events in the Solana Accelerate China 2026 series before they opened and would investigate the domestic entities and individuals involved.
The official described high-profile advertising in Shanghai’s Lujiazui financial district as virtual-currency marketing conducted through local partners.
SOL was characterized as essentially a virtual currency, and the network was noted for supplying technical services used in the issuance and trading of assets such as Tether’s USDT.
Both activities were said to fall outside permissions under a February 2026 multi-agency notice aimed at limiting virtual-currency risks.
The statements reaffirm Beijing’s continued restrictions on foreign public blockchains and related promotional activity, dampening any near-term expectation of policy relaxation.In a separate development, Stellar has recorded the strongest daily expansion in tokenized real-world-asset fund market capitalization among major networks.
Data compiled by the RWA Foundation from Token Terminal showed Stellar’s tokenized funds adding $44.9 million in the 24 hours through November 13, ahead of Solana’s $29 million increase,
Ethereum’s $10.8 million rise, and zkSync Era’s $3.5 million gain.
Stellar ranks second overall for tokenized funds behind Ethereum, with its broader RWA market value reaching approximately $4.67 billion after expanding roughly sixfold over the past year.
The network hosts Franklin Templeton’s BENJI money-market fund, which has operated on Stellar since 2021 as the first U.S.
mutual fund deployed on a public blockchain, along with products from Spiko, Ondo, and WisdomTree.
Compliance-oriented features have drawn traditional asset managers seeking tokenized Treasury and money-market exposure.
These concurrent trends highlight uneven conditions across blockchain ecosystems.
Solana faces concurrent pressure from macro-driven risk aversion, institutional redemptions, large-holder sales, and regulatory friction in a major market, while Stellar is capturing incremental institutional allocation in the tokenized-fund segment.
Whether the mid-$70s zone holds as support for SOL, and whether crypto ETF flows stabilize as broader financial conditions evolve, will be key near-term markers.

polymarket-6507442.text:
In brief
- 21Shares' TSOL product was the sole source of a record $32.19M outflow from Solana ETFs on Wednesday.
- An analyst calls the outflow a likely "position reset" following weeks of inflows and a November drawdown.
- Despite ETF redemptions, over $321M has flowed onto the Solana network in the past month, mostly from Ethereum.
U.S.
spot Solana exchange-traded funds recorded their largest single-day outflow on Wednesday, diverging from a broader crypto market rally led by Bitcoin.
The $32.19 million redemption marks the third—and largest—outflow since the funds launched on October 28, according to SoSoValue data.
A fund breakdown shows the entirety of Wednesday's outflow came from 21Shares’ TSOL product, which saw $41.79 million exit, partially offset by modest inflows into other Solana ETFs.
Notably, TSOL has been the primary source of outflows, contributing to all three Solana ETF redemption events to date.
The previous outflows were $13.55 million on December 1 and $8.10 million on November 26.
“This is likely a position reset after three weeks of uninterrupted inflows and a sharp November drawdown,” Vitaliy Shtyrkin, CPO at an all-in-one crypto ecosystem for business B2BINPAY, told Decrypt.
The outflow coincided with the launch of a competing product, as Franklin Templeton’s Solana ETF (SOEZ) began trading on the same day.
This one was so easy.
Ticker name decider guy here at @FTI_US on an absolute heater this quarter.
Franklin Solana ETF - $SOEZ is now live, making exposure to $SOL almost too easy?
pic.twitter.com/bBA0YfB2LG
— Franklin Templeton Digital Assets (@FTDA_US) December 3, 2025
Despite the ETF weakness, Solana’s on-chain fundamentals tell a different story.
Over $321 million has flowed onto the layer-1 network in the past month, with Ethereum the major contributor, supplying over $240 million of that total, according to Artemis data.
“Since the memecoin peak, on-chain activity has decreased, active addresses fell to multi-month lows, and positioning on derivatives is net-long yet less aggressive than in October,” Shtyrkin added.
This development occurs amid a reduction in exchange supply and stable staking yields.
However, the analyst added, “This doesn’t signal exit, more of a longer-term conviction.”
Solana is currently trading at $142.75, up 1.1% on the day, according to CoinGecko data.
Though Bitcoin’s December 1 selloff and subsequent recovery has relieved near-term pressure, the outlook remains tense due to the Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision on December 10 and economic data releases this month.
Meanwhile, several altcoins have demonstrated strong bounce-back capacity.
Coins like Fartcoin, ZCash, Sui, and PumpFun have posted double-digit rallies over the past week, according to CoinGecko data.
Still, the sentiment remains in the fear territory due to the liquidation spikes noted since October 10.
It will depend on how the macro overhang resolves, particularly in the Fed’s forward guidance for 2026.
Myriad predictors have assigned an 80% chance that Bitcoin will hit $100,000 first before $80,000.

Solana marks 1,000 days without a network halt as activity climbs
Solana logo, official brand asset from solana.com/branding.
Alpenglow is a Solana consensus upgrade.
The blockchain has produced blocks nonstop since February 2024, while DEX volume and transactions doubled and active traders grew sixfold
Solana has now gone 1,000 consecutive days without a network halt.
Its last full stoppage happened on February 6, 2024.
The streak reached 1,000 days of 100% cluster-level uptime around November 2, 2026.
The cluster is the full set of validators that run the network together, so this measures the chain as a whole, not one machine.
In the months before the milestone, Solana’s status page showed 100% uptime.
The stability did not come during a lull.
Over the same period, average monthly DEX volume on Solana has doubled compared with February 2024.
Total transactions processed on the network have also doubled across that timeframe.
The standout figure involves people, not throughput.
The number of active traders on Solana has grown sixfold from levels seen before the February 2024 halt.
What broke in 2024, and what changed
The February 6, 2024 outage stemmed from a bug in validator software.
Specifically, the code got stuck in an infinite recompile loop, repeatedly redoing the same work without moving forward.
The halt lasted approximately five hours.
Since then, several upgrades have been credited with making the network sturdier.
The most prominent is Firedancer, a second independent validator client developed by Jump Crypto.
The news moving money, markets, and the world—before your day starts.

Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy.
A validator client is the software that nodes run to process transactions and agree on the chain’s state.
With only one client, a single bug can take down every node at once, which is roughly what happened in 2024.
A second, separately written client changes that math.
If one program trips over a flaw, nodes running the other may keep going.
Solana also rolled out improved protocols aimed at curbing spam and congestion.
A newly introduced priority-fee market rounds out the list.
Users can pay extra to move their transactions ahead in line, giving the network a pricing signal to sort urgent traffic from noise.
Engineers have kept pushing on speed during the streak.
On August 21, 2026, slot time dropped to 350 milliseconds, with plans to push it further toward 200 ms.
Not entirely incident-free
The streak has not meant zero problems.
In August 2026, an infrastructure routing failure temporarily affected 29% of stake.
Block production continued anyway.
Outside data broadly backs the stability picture.
A report from the Fidelity Center for Applied Technology found vote success rates near 99.7% throughout 2026.
The same Fidelity report also flagged concerns.
It pointed to issues with how stake is distributed across validators and with the diversity of providers hosting them.
What this means for Solana and its users
Still, the August 2026 routing failure is a useful reminder of where risk now sits.
When 29% of stake can be knocked sideways by one infrastructure problem, the network’s health depends heavily on a small number of hosting setups.
That ties directly to the decentralization questions in the Fidelity report.
A network can post excellent uptime numbers while still concentrating stake and hosting in ways that create shared points of failure.
The push toward 200 ms slot times adds another variable.
Faster blocks are attractive for trading, but every speed gain narrows the margin validators have to stay in sync.

Solana comes close to halting after 29% of staked SOL goes offline
A routing failure at infrastructure provider Teraswitch sent roughly 90 validators offline and pushed delinquent stake close to Solana's 33.34% finality threshold.
Solana came close to losing transaction finality on Wednesday after a routing failure at infrastructure provider Teraswitch caused 28.83% of the network’s staked SOL to become delinquent.
The disruption brought Solana to roughly 86% of the 33.34% delinquent stake threshold at which the network would no longer have the two thirds supermajority required to finalize transactions.
The network continued operating during the incident.
Around 90 validators were affected, collectively missing an estimated 333 SOL in staking rewards.
The missed rewards are expected to be covered by validator bonds at the end of the epoch.
The incident originated from a routing fault at Teraswitch.
According to the provider’s account of the event, a default route from its Miami site was advertised without the expected attributes.
A route reflector in Amsterdam then distributed the route across Teraswitch locations in Europe and Asia Pacific.
Edge routers at the affected locations preferred the incorrect route while the underlying core network rejected it as invalid, leaving 12 sites without a valid forwarding route.
Locations affected included sites in London, Amsterdam, Dublin, Frankfurt, Singapore, and Tokyo.
North American locations were not affected.

Teraswitch identified the issue within around 10 minutes, with traffic restored by 04:16:15 UTC.
Some validators remained offline longer, with certain operators experiencing around 33 minutes of downtime.
The incident also exposed the concentration of Solana validator infrastructure among individual network providers.
Autonomous system AS20326, operated by Teraswitch, hosted approximately 118.9 million SOL in stake, with about 94% of that stake going offline simultaneously during the disruption.
Additional validators hosted through Latitude.sh, Limestone, Butterfly Research, and Allnodes also became delinquent during the same period, accounting for roughly another 14.1 million SOL, according to the analysis.
Marinade said 59 validators representing roughly 80.2 million SOL recovered within the same narrow period as routing service returned across Amsterdam, Frankfurt, and Tokyo, indicating that the affected validators had remained offline until network connectivity was restored rather than switching to alternative infrastructure.
The incident occurred just days after Solana reached 30 consecutive months without a network wide outage.
Its last full halt occurred in February 2024, when validators had to coordinate a manual restart that took close to five hours.

China’s Central Bank to Investigate Solana Promotion in Shanghai
China's central bank to investigate Solana promotion.
The People’s Bank of China (PBoC), in collaboration with other agencies, will investigate organizations and individuals involved in promoting Solana in the country.
This was announced by the head of the relevant regulatory department in an interview with a Chinese newspaper.
The investigation was prompted by advertising of the blockchain on the facade of Citigroup Tower in Shanghai’s Lujiazui financial district.
According to the official, the project used local companies to promote cryptocurrencies by popularizing the brand.
A PBoC representative confirmed that the central bank, along with local financial departments, police, and market supervision authorities, halted the offline events of Solana Accelerate China 2026.
These were planned to be held in Shanghai and other cities.
The regulator linked its decision to a notice from eight departments published in February 2026.
The document classifies cryptocurrency business within the country as illegal financial activity and holds local organizations and citizens accountable for facilitating such services for foreign entities.
Furthermore, a ban on mining has been in effect in mainland China since 2021.
The official described Solana as a major blockchain platform, noting that SOL is a virtual currency and the network provides technical services for issuing and trading USDT and other crypto assets.
“This falls under the illegal financial activities defined in the notice.
The promotion of Solana already violates its provisions,” stated the PBoC representative.
The regulator cited issues with client identification, anti-money laundering efforts, and the risk of speculation.
The PBoC intends to continue cracking down on cryptocurrency businesses within the country, focusing on local trading companies and foreign blockchain platforms based in China.
In September 2026, China’s Ministry of State Security warned citizens about the risks of cryptocurrencies.
The agency also stated that the anonymity of crypto transactions is an “illusion.”

US Spot XRP ETFs See Largest Weekly Outflows in 8 Months as XRP Falls Below $1
U.S.
spot XRP exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $19.13 million in net outflows during November 9–13, 2026, marking their largest weekly withdrawal in eight months.
The decline coincided with broader cryptocurrency market weakness, as XRP subsequently fell below the psychologically important $1 level.
Grayscale and Bitwise accounted for most of the ETF withdrawals, while Franklin Templeton attracted fresh capital.
Despite the negative flows, cumulative ETF inflows remain near $1.79 billion.
The divergence between short-term redemptions and longer-term investment demand raises questions about institutional sentiment, market liquidity, and XRP's near-term outlook.
Key Takeaways
-
U.S.
spot XRP ETFs recorded $19.13 million in weekly net outflows during November 9–13, their largest weekly withdrawal since March 2026 and the second consecutive week of negative flows.
-
Grayscale's GXRP led redemptions with approximately $12.71 million, followed by Bitwise's XRP ETF with $9.40 million, while Franklin Templeton's XRPZ attracted $4.45 million.
-
Combined XRP ETF net assets fell approximately 14% to $1.15 billion, but most of the decline reflected falling asset valuations rather than investor withdrawals.
-
XRP slipped below $1 during the weekend following the reporting period, amid broader cryptocurrency weakness and deteriorating short-term market sentiment.
-
Cumulative ETF net inflows remain near $1.79 billion, indicating that the latest withdrawals represent a short-term reversal rather than evidence of a complete institutional exit.
What Happened to US Spot XRP ETFs in November 2026?
U.S.-listed spot XRP ETFs experienced their largest weekly net withdrawal in eight months during the trading week ending November 13, 2026.
According to SoSoValue data, the funds recorded approximately $19.13 million in aggregate net outflows, their second consecutive negative week.
The withdrawal was the largest since March 2026 and ranked among the four biggest weekly outflow periods since U.S.
spot XRP ETFs began launching in November 2025.
The figures indicate weakening short-term demand through exchange-traded investment products, although they do not establish that investors are abandoning XRP as an asset.
The selling was heavily concentrated in the first two sessions.
On November 9, U.S.
spot XRP ETFs recorded approximately $10.42 million in net outflows, their largest daily withdrawal since early March.
Another $7.62 million left on November 10, while November 11 and 12 showed no reported net changes.
The week ended with an additional $1.09 million in withdrawals on November 13.
Together, the first two trading days accounted for approximately 94% of the weekly net outflow, suggesting that the decline was driven by a relatively concentrated period of selling rather than five consecutive days of substantial redemptions.

The escrow consists of independent on ledger escrows that release a total of one billion XRP each month over the next 55 months.
Any additional XRP leftover each month will be placed into a new escrow to release in the first month in which no escrow currently releases.

To provide additional predictability to the XRP supply, Ripple has locked 55 billion XRP (55% of the total possible supply) into a series of escrows.
These escrows are on the ledger itself and the ledger mechanics, enforced by consensus, control the release of the XRP.
The escrow consists of independent on ledger escrows that release a total of one billion XRP each month over the next 55 months.
This provides an upper limit on the amount of new XRP that can be brought into circulation.
The amount of XRP actually released into circulation will likely be much less than this.
Any additional XRP leftover each month will be placed into a new escrow to release in the first month in which no escrow currently releases.
During the process of moving Ripple’s XRP into escrow, we also changed our account security model.
The XRP Ledger supports a native multisign scheme and Ripple secured the accounts the escrows release into using this scheme.
The multisignature scheme has numerous advantages over the schemes other ledgers use.
For example, the signers or quorum can be changed without changing the receiving address.
Individual signers can rotate their own credentials without disturbing the funds on the ledger.
Ledger Mechanics
The XRP Ledger’s escrow system is designed to handle two use cases.
The one that gives it its name is its ability to lock funds on the ledger subject to release to one of two accounts depending on whether a particular condition occurs by a particular time.
This supports Interledger transactions or cross-ledger atomic swaps.

Escrows are created with an “EscrowCreate” transaction.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on Wednesday, above the expected range, setting the stage for the Claude creator's eagerly awaited Nasdaq listing and a historic moment for the artificial intelligence industry.
The company, along with its seven co-founders, upsized the offering, selling about 980 million shares, according to a press release.
That brings the amount raised to $81.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June.
Elon Musk's company raised $75 billion initially and a total of $85.7 billion after underwriters exercised their overallotment.

Epic Games is one of the biggest names in gaming, but its private market shares are telling a more cautious story.
The Forge Price for Epic Games stood at $328.86 per share as of Sept.
14, down 26.92% over the past year and 31.45% over the past six months, according to Forge Global data.
Epic is not publicly traded, and the Forge Price is a derived private market price rather than a conventional stock-market quote.
The decline comes as Epic faces pressure around Fortnite engagement and attempts to bring its costs more in line with its business.
Epic’s recent private-market performance comes after a significant valuation reset.
The company reached a $31.5 billion valuation in April 2022, when Sony Group Corp (NYSE:SONY) and Kirkbi, the family investment group behind Lego, each invested $1 billion in Epic.
Less than two years later, Epic’s valuation had fallen.
In February 2024, Walt Disney Co (NYSE:DIS) invested $1.5 billion in the company in a transaction that valued Epic at $22.5 billion, according to private market data.
That represented roughly a 29% decline from Epic’s 2022 valuation benchmark.
The current Forge Price adds another layer to that valuation story.
While Forge’s price is not directly comparable to a primary funding-round valuation, its nearly 27% one-year decline shows sentiment in the private secondary market has weakened further.
Fortnite remains a key driver of Epic’s business — and a growing source of concern for investors.
In March, CEO Tim Sweeney told employees that a downturn in Fortnite engagement that began in 2025 meant Epic was "spending significantly more than we’re making." The company announced more than 1,000 layoffs and said it had identified more than $500 million in savings through reductions in contracting, marketing and open positions.
The cuts followed another major round of layoffs in 2023, when Epic eliminated roughly 830 positions.
While Fortnite continues to attract a massive audience, engagement has weakened.
Reuters reported that while Fortnite remained among the most-played games, average playtime had fallen, creating a challenge for a live-service business that depends on keeping players engaged and spending.
That makes the private market decline particularly notable.
Investors aren’t necessarily betting against Fortnite itself; they may be reassessing how much future growth can be generated from a franchise that has already reached enormous scale.
Epic has been trying to build a business that extends beyond Fortnite, including through Unreal Engine, the Epic Games Store and its creator ecosystem.
The company has also been pushing toward a broader vision in which Fortnite functions more like a platform than a single game, giving creators more ways to build experiences and monetize content.
That strategy could ultimately help Epic diversify its revenue and reduce its dependence on the engagement cycle of one blockbuster title.
But for now, the private market numbers suggest investors are taking a more cautious view.

Case Study: Kernel Optimization
We tested the model's ability to iteratively optimize GPU kernels over 1,000+ tool calls (up to 24 hours).
Leveraging Muse Code's agentic coding environment, the model writes, compiles, profiles, and progressively improves kernel performance relative to a provided baseline implementation.
We benchmarked on KDA and MLA kernels for NVIDIA Hopper GPUs.
The agent continues to achieve substantial improvements over the provided baseline implementation.
The baseline is the FLA Triton implementation of KDA.
Models were prohibited from importing third-party kernel libraries such as FLA directly; instead, they had to apply specialized kernel-optimization knowledge to implement the algorithm in Triton, rather than wrap existing implementations.
Muse Spark 1.2 paired a chunk-parallel preparation kernel with a sequential inter-chunk scan, combining standard fusion and tiling with KDA-specific optimizations such as re-centering the gated cumulative decay at the chunk midpoint.

Facebook's parent company on Thursday updated its Muse Spark large language model and followed through on a promise to make it available to developers.
Why it matters: It's a busy period for model upgrades across the industry, with OpenAI and SpaceXAI also debuting faster models this week.
Driving the news: Muse Spark 1.1 promises improvements in coding and handling longer tasks.
Muse Spark, the first large language model developed under Alexandr Wang, already powers a wide range of tasks across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Meta AI.
With this version, developers can also tap the model via an API (Application Programming Interface).
Meta says it believes its model is priced attractively given its capabilities, charging customers $1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 per million output tokens.
(That's cheaper than the new Grok 4.5, and also less than Anthropic's Opus model.)
What they're saying: Wang, who was brought in to reboot Meta's AI effort, told Axios that improving Muse Spark's performance in coding and agentic tasks was a key focus with this release.
"These were priority areas for us," he said.
Meta is also using the model to power the thinking mode in the Meta AI app and website.
The big picture: Meta is trying to close the gap between it and AI leaders including OpenAI and Anthropic.
The company is promising a significantly more powerful version of Spark later this year that uses substantially more computing power.
Earlier this week, Meta debuted Muse Image, a picture-generating model that has been added to Meta AI and powers new image editing features in Instagram.
This is not the big leap that Meta hopes to make with its next big release.
Code-named Watermelon, that model is still in training and uses vastly more compute and should be released later this year.
What's next: Longer term, Wang said he is working toward a vision where a more agentic Meta AI could handle tasks like planning a party or a vacation and take more direct actions on its own.
Wang said Meta's strength is its billions of users and how much the company knows about them.
"That's really the part that no one else can replicate," he said.

Muse Spark Open is available today and brings leading agentic capabilities to your desktop for the first time on Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios.
Today, we’re releasing the weights for Muse Spark Open, the most capable US open-weight model to date.
Muse Spark Open is a natively multimodal model with 816B total parameters (42B active) and a 1M-token context window.
Built for coding and agentic work, it excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning.
We believe the future is for everyone, and that includes the freedom to run advanced models wherever, including at home.
Muse Spark Open is the first model in its class to run on your desktop using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios with the latest MLX framework.
Muse Spark Open is available today through API platforms at Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together AI.
Model weights are available for download on Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden, Hugging Face, and Microsoft Foundry Models.
It runs on leading inference engines like SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Hugging Face Transformers, Apple MLX, llama.cpp, and Unsloth with optimizations for AMD, Apple, Intel, and NVIDIA silicon.
Developers can easily further customize the model using the PyTorch framework.
Key Benchmarks
For more details about our evaluations, see the evaluation methodology report.
Optimized for Apple Silicon
Leveraging the latest version of MLX, Muse Spark Open was optimized to run on Mac Studio with M5 Ultra, and together they’re the best way to run a powerful model on your own desktop.
Apple’s unified memory architecture lets the M5 Ultra's integrated GPU use up to 512 GB per Mac Studio, so two machines can hold an entire model.
And the chip’s 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth is fast enough to read the small slice each token needs.
The result is two Mac Studios behave like one supercomputer with a terabyte of unified memory.
We tested a range of agentic workflows running entirely on-device, using Muse Code powered by Muse Spark Open, including shipping real iOS chang
[...]
an open-source Mastodon client) — bug fixes, new features, full build — and driving DaVinci Resolve end to end, with the model reviewing footage frame by frame to find the strongest moments and crop them vertically.
Available Now
We’re sharing this work because we want everyone to have access to the best models.
The open-weight version of Muse Spark ships with custom, auto-tunable Helion GPU kernels in SGLang, delivering 1.03-3.95× kernel-level speedups on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, and a 3% end-to-end speedup on AMD MI350.
Safety and Preparedness
Releasing open-weight models is part of how we bring the benefits of personal superintelligence to everyone, and part of how safety work advances across the field.
Open weights also carry their own considerations, and Muse Spark Open has additional safety post-training for that reason.
The results demonstrate strong safeguards across risk categories measured.
We evaluated the model in line with our Meta Superintelligence Scaling Framework, covering the most severe risks, and it met the thresholds our framework requires for release.
Detailed results are in the Muse Spark Open model card, with a full evaluation report available soon.
License
We’re releasing the weights under the Muse Model License with limited commercial terms, which allow many developers to use the model for free.
Get Started
You can customize Muse Spark Open for your use case by leveraging PyTorch’s TorchTitan to further tune the model.
To run it on Apple silicon, use MLX, which pulls the weights directly from Hugging Face.

The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Nov.
13, 2026, after severe network data flooding triggered instability across air traffic facilities, according to agency officials.
The system disruption began at approximately 3:30 p.m.
Eastern time and affected 17 of 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers, as well as several Terminal Radar Approach Control facilities.
Controllers maintained contact with airborne flights via backup frequencies and radar feeds, allowing approximately 3,500 aircraft in the sky to land safely before operations resumed at 8:15 p.m.
Airlines canceled more than 12,400 flights during the disruption.
According to FAA officials, the instability began when legacy telecommunications equipment was flooded with data at a rate of 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds.
An initial investigation identified two originating locations: A radar site in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio communications facility in El Dorado, Arkansas.
Network service provider L3Harris had been deploying a new router at the Arkansas site when the issue occurred, according to FAA officials.
Technicians stabilized the network by blocking traffic from both locations and disabling the broadcasting function on approximately 60 similar routers across the system.
Officials confirmed there was no indication of a cyberattack, and “critical life-saving, law enforcement, and military operations continued without disruption.”
For more information: NasStatus.FAA.gov, FAA.gov

FAA grounds flights nationwide, citing communications outage
The U.S.
Federal Aviation Administration grounded all departing flights nationwide after a communications failure hit air traffic control centers.
The U.S.
Federal Aviation Administration grounded all departing flights nationwide on Friday after a communications failure hit air traffic control centers, in only the second such shutdown since the Sept.
11, 2001, attacks.
Nearly 7,000 flights were delayed or canceled, according to flight-tracking service FlightAware.
Planes already in the air were allowed to land, but those on the ground could not take off.
The disruption is the latest and most dramatic sign of strain on a U.S.
air traffic control system beset by equipment and communications failures, controller shortages and aging infrastructure.
“The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S.
airports following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.
FAA technicians are investigating the issue.
We will provide immediate updates as we have them,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a post on X.
Airline officials said the FAA had not indicated when the ground stop might be lifted, but there were preliminary indications the communications issues were improving in some places.
The world’s busiest airspace has experienced setbacks in recent years that have disrupted flights and risked safety.
In January 2025, a midair collision at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport killed 67 people.
The White House and Department of Transportation urged Congress on Friday to approve a further $30.1 billion to upgrade the United States’ aging airports and air traffic control system.
Aviation security concerns
The FAA announced the nationwide ground stop at 3:54 p.m ET (2054 GMT).
Shortly before the announcement, the FAA halted traffic in Chicago due to air traffic control communications issues.
“If the ground stop continues through the evening, it likely will take the weekend to resolve the disruptions to airlines’ networks,” said Robert Mann, an aviation analyst and principal of R.W.
Mann & Co.
The only other nationwide ground stop since the Sept.
11 attacks came in January 2023, when the FAA halted domestic departures for less than two hours.
The outage comes amid heightened concern about aviation security worldwide after a wave of hoax bomb threats this month disrupted dozens of passenger flights across Europe, forcing unscheduled landings and prompting fighter jets to escort or intercept aircraft.
There was no immediate indication the U.S.
communications failure was related to those incidents or caused by a cyberattack.
The U.S.
National Weather Service also said on Friday it was experiencing nationwide internet and communications issues.
There was no immediate indication the two incidents were connected.
